summary: Nineteen named reference universes expose recurring genome and community questions through curated metadata filters
rationale: Users could already construct universes from type, mode, facets and the derived GIFT profile, but every analysis had to restate biologically meaningful groupings and their interpretation limits. Storing reusable filter recipes makes those groupings discoverable and versioned while preserving the rule that a universe is never a hard-coded list of GIFT identifiers.
evidence: Existing curated gift_type, mode, gift_facet and gift_profile semantics in database release 2026.20.3; quantitative-trait invariants and implemented metrics documented in inst/doc/proposal-quantitative-traits.md.
effect: No GIFT, route, architecture, circuit, mechanism, marker or Boolean call changes. Schema version 7 adds normalized reference-universe definitions, filters and metric recommendations. Nineteen presets resolve membership from current metadata; only biomass-essential anabolism and its amino-acid, nucleotide and cofactor subsets are declared bounded.

summary: Ectoine biosynthesis and choline-to-betaine oxidation are curated as bounded compatible-solute chemistry
rationale: The claims end at L-ectoine and glycine betaine and deliberately exclude transport, regulation, intracellular concentration and osmotic-tolerance outcomes. The ectoine cut starts at the existing ASA branchpoint instead of repeating its upstream trunk. Choline oxidation reuses the existing BETAINE anchor and admits four chemically complete routes, while refusing ALDH7A1 K14085 because its aldehyde range cannot identify betaine aldehyde.
evidence: Rhea release 141; KEGG M00033 and M00555; MetaCyc P101-PWY, BETSYN-PWY and PWY-3722; ectoine biochemistry PMID 31921013 and GbsAB genetics PMID 8752328, all assessed 2026-08-20. Full boundary and marker audit in inst/doc/proposal-compatible-solutes-heme-enterobactin-detoxification.md.
effect: ectoine_biosynthesis becomes callable only on EctB plus EctA plus EctC. choline_to_betaine becomes callable on BetA/BetB, GbsB/GbsA, choline-monooxygenase/BADH or choline oxidase and composes into the existing betaine chain. K14085 fires neither.

summary: Heme b biosynthesis is curated from the uroporphyrinogen III branchpoint through classical and coproporphyrin routes
rationale: UROGEN_III is the last shared anchor before corrin, siroheme and heme chemistry diverge. Six classical minimal routes materialise independent HemF/HemN and HemY/HemG/HemJ choices, and a seventh route represents the HemY-HemH-HemQ coproporphyrin pathway. Multifunctional HemY and HemH markers attach to two reaction-specific components. The siroheme route is excluded because it has a different input boundary.
evidence: Rhea release 141; KEGG M00121 and M00926; MetaCyc HEME-BIOSYNTHESIS-II, HEMESYN2-PWY and PWY-7766; HemG PMID 19583219, HemJ PMID 20823222 and the coproporphyrin route PMID 25646457, assessed 2026-08-20.
effect: heme_b_biosynthesis becomes callable on any complete route. A partial route, a ferrochelatase alone or siroheme-pathway markers remain negative. The new HEME_B anchor does not make a vitamin or respiratory-capacity claim.

summary: Enterobactin biosynthesis is split at 2,3-dihydroxybenzoate into a reusable catecholate head and a complete assembly GIFT
rationale: MetaCyc ENTBACSYN-PWY crosses a useful branchpoint. Curating its head once prevents reaction duplication and lets other catecholate products reuse it. The tail uses the aggregate Rhea EC 6.3.2.14 reaction but keeps EntB, EntD, EntE and EntF as four jointly required system components; EntB's lyase and carrier roles remain separate despite sharing one marker.
evidence: Rhea release 141 RHEA:18985, RHEA:11112, RHEA:23824 and RHEA:30571; KEGG map01053 and K01252/K00216/K02362/K02363/K02364; MetaCyc ENTBACSYN-PWY; assembly enzymology PMID 10375542, assessed 2026-08-20.
effect: dihydroxybenzoate_biosynthesis composes from the existing chorismate output into enterobactin_biosynthesis through the new DIHYDROXYBENZOATE_2_3 anchor. The head can be positive without the tail; the tail requires all four assembly components and claims neither secretion nor iron acquisition.

summary: Two complete chemical-detoxification mechanisms are added for methylglyoxal and superoxide
rationale: Methylglyoxal disposal requires both glutathione-dependent glyoxalases and stops at D-lactate, before its oxidation. Superoxide detoxification requires removal of both superoxide and the hydrogen peroxide produced; SOD alone is incomplete. Alternative catalases and the complete AhpC-AhpF pair satisfy peroxide removal. Nickel SOD without its maturation protease, superoxide reductase without its electron-delivery architecture, and broad methylglyoxal reductases are not accepted.
evidence: Rhea release 141 RHEA:19069, RHEA:25245, RHEA:20696, RHEA:20309 and RHEA:62620; MetaCyc PWY-5386, DETOX1-PWY and DETOX1-PWY-1; PMID 21143325, PMID 22609271, PMID 15516600 and PMID 12072973, assessed 2026-08-20.
effect: methylglyoxal_detoxification becomes callable only on GloA plus GloB. superoxide_detoxification becomes callable only on an accepted SOD plus an accepted catalase or both AhpC and AhpF. SOD alone, K00518 and K05919 remain negative.

summary: Polyhydroxybutyrate biosynthesis is refused at the current marker specificity
rationale: The proposed acetyl-CoA-to-PHB boundary is coherent, but K03821 identifies polyhydroxyalkanoate synthases spanning different monomer and chain-length preferences. PhaA and PhaB context establishes 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA supply but cannot make the downstream polymerase accession PHB-specific, so a positive call would exceed its genomic evidence.
evidence: Rhea release 141 RHEA:15405 and RHEA:66924; KEGG K00626, K00023 and K03821; PhaC specificity studies PMID 15205419, PMID 24564904 and PMID 21261834, assessed 2026-08-20. Full audit in inst/doc/proposal-compatible-solutes-heme-enterobactin-detoxification.md.
effect: No PHB GIFT, polymer anchor, route or marker is added. Reconsider only when a maintained marker can distinguish a synthase accepting 3-hydroxybutyrate at the claimed polymer specificity, such as a validated class-specific custom HMM.

summary: Siroheme biosynthesis is curated from uroporphyrinogen III through multifunctional or split enzyme systems
rationale: Siroheme is a defensible cofactor branchpoint between uroporphyrinogen III and siroheme-dependent chemistry. The route requires methylation, dehydrogenation and iron insertion. CysG supplies all three; Met8 supplies the terminal pair; split systems require an accepted methyltransferase, SirC and iron-specific SirB. RHEA:32459 consolidates the two sequential methyl transfers that MetaCyc records separately, so the route has three Rhea reactions without collapsing two different genomic requirements.
evidence: Rhea release 141 RHEA:32459, RHEA:15613 and RHEA:24360; ChEBI release 253 CHEBI:60052; KEGG M00846 and K00589/K02302/K02303/K02304/K02496/K03794/K13542/K13543/K24866; MetaCyc 30.0 PWY-5194; PMID 9461500, PMID 11980703 and PMID 12408752, verified 2026-08-20. The accepted markers complete the UROGEN_III-to-siroheme tail in 4161 of 10151 bacterial and 1 of 470 archaeal KEGG genomes.
effect: siroheme_biosynthesis becomes callable on CysG alone or a complete split implementation and exposes the SIROHEME branchpoint. CbiX-family evidence that cannot resolve iron insertion remains negative, so the trait knowingly under-calls archaeal alternatives. No siroheme-dependent reductase, alternative heme route, cofactor use or phenotype is implied.

summary: Siroheme-to-heme b remains refused because KO K22225 cannot prove both AhbA and AhbB
rationale: The siroheme-to-heme boundary and its three chemical reactions are coherent, and AhbC plus either AhbD or the peroxide-dependent heme synthase are product-specific. The first reaction nevertheless requires the AhbA-AhbB heterodimer. KEGG assigns both experimentally required Methanosarcina genes to K22225, so putting that accession on two components would let one observed gene satisfy both and would collapse a multisubunit system. Gene order cannot repair the evidence, and gifter has no marker-multiplicity contract.
evidence: MetaCyc 30.0 PWY-7552; Rhea release 141 RHEA:19093, RHEA:37431, RHEA:56520 and RHEA:56516; KEGG M00847 and Mbar_A1459/Mbar_A1460, both K22225; PMID 24669201 and PMID 24865947. Of the current KEGG genomes carrying the full K22225-K22226-(K22227 or K25033) expression, 45 bacterial and 3 archaeal genomes have only one K22225 gene row, verified 2026-08-20.
effect: No siroheme_to_heme_b GIFT, route or Ahb marker is added, and the existing heme_b_biosynthesis boundary remains UROGEN_III through the classical routes. Reconsider only with maintained markers that distinguish AhbA from AhbB, a validated fusion-specific marker, or a general evidence contract that requires distinct observed genes for repeated accessions.

summary: Initial curated release of five nucleotide biosynthesis GIFTs
rationale: Establish the reference content of gifter as biologically bounded capabilities between declared molecular anchors, derived from but not equal to KEGG modules M00048 to M00052.
evidence: Rhea release 141 reaction chemistry, ChEBI release 253 anchor identity, KEGG modules M00048-M00052 for pathway organisation and orthology assignment.
effect: Baseline release. Purine core, adenylate, guanylate, pyrimidine core and cytidylate biosynthesis become callable, composing through the shared IMP anchor.

summary: Aspartate carbamoyltransferase no longer requires the PyrI regulatory subunit
rationale: PyrI is an allosteric regulator, not a catalytic subunit, and class C aspartate carbamoyltransferases are catalytic trimers with no regulatory subunit. Requiring K00610 asserted a subunit that most prokaryotes do not encode. The previous definition followed the KEGG module expression (K00609+K00610,K00608), which is a pathway drawing convention rather than an evidence claim.
evidence: Of 9670 KEGG organisms carrying K00609, 7863 carry neither K00610 nor K00608. Bacillus subtilis, Lactococcus lactis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, all de novo pyrimidine prototrophs, were called incomplete at RHEA:20013 when evaluated from their complete KEGG orthology annotation.
effect: SYS_20013_HOLOENZYME became the single-component SYS_20013_CATALYTIC, satisfied by K00609 alone; COMP_20013_REGULATORY and marker K00610 were removed. Those five reference genomes now complete the GIFT; no genome lost a previously complete call.

summary: NAD-dependent dihydroorotate oxidation now requires the PyrK electron transfer subunit
rationale: The class 1B enzyme is a PyrDb/PyrK holoenzyme. The catalytic subunit alone cannot reduce NAD+, so accepting K17828 by itself claimed the NAD-dependent chemistry from half of the enzyme. KEGG module M00051 lists only K17828 for this step.
evidence: KEGG annotates K02823 (pyrDII/PyrK) to the same reaction R01869 as K17828, and 2403 of the 2724 organisms carrying K17828 also carry K02823.
effect: SYS_13513_NAD gained the required component COMP_13513_ELECTRON accepting K02823. Genomes annotated with K17828 but not K02823 now report RHEA:13513 as unsupported and fall back to the fumarate-dependent or quinone-dependent route. None of the nine reference genomes changed.

summary: Marker layer audited against KEGG orthology; no orthologs missing
rationale: Confirm whether other genomic markers are acceptable for the curated enzymes before broadening the evidence layer, and record the rejected candidates so they are not re-proposed.
evidence: The accepted markers of all 27 reactions were compared against every KO that KEGG assigns to the corresponding EC number, and against the step logic of modules M00048-M00052. Twenty-six of 27 reactions matched exactly; the only difference was the regulatory K00610 retired in this release.
effect: No markers added. K06863 stays off the folate-dependent AICAR transformylase because purP is formate-dependent and modelled as RHEA:24836. K01948 (EC 6.3.4.16) remains unacceptable for the glutamine-dependent RHEA:18633. Non-KO namespaces validate and resolve correctly but were not adopted, because evaluation has no confidence filter and weaker evidence would silently change calls.

summary: Curation history recorded inside the database and published in the atlas
rationale: Database decisions were only readable in a Markdown file next to the code. Storing them as curated source tables keeps the biological history versioned with the content it describes, linked to the GIFTs it affects, and publishable with the reference atlas.
evidence: Schema version 2 adds database_change and change_gift; sources are database_changes.tsv and change_gifts.tsv.
effect: No change to any GIFT call. database_changelog() reads the history, the HTML atlas gains a Changelog view, and each GIFT shows its own change history.

summary: Nine serine, glycine, aspartate-family, cysteine and methionine biosynthesis GIFTs added
rationale: Extend gifter beyond nucleotide metabolism with the amino acid capabilities most often needed to interpret host-associated genomes, curated as bounded capabilities rather than as imported KEGG modules.
evidence: KEGG modules M00016-M00021, M00338 and M00609 for orthology and pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for reaction identity, direction and ChEBI participants; KEGG gene-to-organism links for the prevalence figures quoted in the accompanying change entries.
effect: Eleven anchors, nine GIFTs, nineteen routes and twenty-five reactions become callable. The amino acid GIFTs compose into a single acyclic chain from 3-phosphoglycerate through serine and cysteine to methionine, and from aspartate through the semialdehyde and homoserine branchpoints to threonine and methionine.

summary: The aspartate-to-homoserine trunk is curated once instead of twice
rationale: KEGG M00018 and M00017 both contain aspartate kinase, aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase and homoserine dehydrogenase. Importing both modules as GIFTs would encode the same three reactions twice and let the two copies drift apart. The trunk is cut at the two real branchpoints instead.
evidence: 6569 KEGG organisms satisfy the orthology of both modules, so the duplication would be exercised in the majority of genomes carrying either. L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde is the branchpoint to lysine and diaminopimelate (M00016); L-homoserine is the branchpoint to threonine and methionine and is named in both module titles.
effect: aspartate_semialdehyde_biosynthesis and homoserine_biosynthesis carry the shared chemistry; threonine and methionine biosynthesis begin at the homoserine anchor and compose through it. The lysine and diaminopimelate branch can later attach at the semialdehyde anchor without re-cutting any existing GIFT.

summary: Direct sulfhydrylation added as a methionine biosynthesis capability absent from KEGG M00017
rationale: M00017 models only transsulfuration, in which cysteine donates the sulfur through cystathionine. Many prokaryotes instead incorporate inorganic sulfide directly into acylated homoserine. Following the module would call those genomes methionine auxotrophs.
evidence: Among KEGG organisms carrying the complete aspartate-to-homoserine trunk and a homoserine acyltransferase, 4096 have only a direct sulfhydrylase, 985 have only the transsulfuration enzymes and 2353 have both. 3910 organisms complete methionine biosynthesis by sulfhydrylation and would be called incomplete by M00017 as written.
effect: methionine_biosynthesis_sulfhydrylation was created with the sulfide input anchor declared. It is kept separate from the transsulfuration capability because anchors are declared per GIFT and not per route, so one GIFT declaring both cysteine and sulfide inputs would over-claim the requirements of both routes.

summary: M00338 and the cysteine-forming tail of M00609 merged; the SAM-cycle steps of M00609 excluded
rationale: The first four steps of M00609 are the activated methyl cycle, not cysteine biosynthesis. K17462 is a putative AdoMet-dependent methyltransferase with EC 2.1.1.- whose reaction R10404 has no Rhea master, and the SAM-to-SAH conversion it stands for is performed by hundreds of unrelated methyltransferases. Requiring it is a pathway-drawing convention, as K00610 was for aspartate carbamoyltransferase. The remaining two steps make cysteine from homocysteine, which is exactly what M00338 does by different chemistry.
evidence: Of 489 KEGG organisms carrying both K17216 and K17217, only 332 carry K17462, so 157 would be called incomplete for a step that is not evidence of anything. None of the 2592 organisms carrying the M00338 pair K01697 and K01758 carries the M00609 pair, which makes the two enzyme sets taxonomically disjoint solutions to one problem rather than two traits.
effect: cysteine_biosynthesis_homocysteine carries both chemistries as the alternative routes CYS_RT_SERINE and CYS_RT_OAS. The O-acetyl-L-serine route additionally requires serine O-acetyltransferase, which M00609 omits because its diagram enters at O-acetyl-L-serine; 486 of the 489 organisms carry it, so the added requirement costs almost no sensitivity.

summary: L-homocysteine is declared as an input anchor only, and methionine biosynthesis is not split at it
rationale: Cysteine to methionine and homocysteine to cysteine is a real metabolic interconversion, so the obvious boundary choices make the anchor-derived composition graph cyclic and the database fails to build. Declaring homocysteine as an output anchor, or curating a methionine-to-homocysteine GIFT, re-creates the cycle.
evidence: The source validator turns every output-anchor to input-anchor match into a directed edge and rejects cycles. With homocysteine as an output the graph closes through METHIONINE, HOMOCYSTEINE and CYSTEINE. In the organisms that use the mcc route the homocysteine consumed by cysteine biosynthesis comes from methionine salvage rather than from de novo methionine biosynthesis, so an input-only boundary is also the honest one.
effect: L-homocysteine stays internal to both methionine GIFTs and is declared only as an input of cysteine_biosynthesis_homocysteine. Any future methionine salvage or SAM-cycle GIFT must revisit this boundary before it can be added.

summary: GIFTs can be linked to related external pathways with an explicit set relation
rationale: A GIFT is a curated capability between declared anchors and is deliberately not equal to any pathway record, but users arrive from the resources they already know. A reference that only named a module would imply an equivalence that is usually false, so the link stores how the boundaries compare.
evidence: Schema version 3 adds gift_xref with the relation vocabulary equivalent, subset_of, superset_of, overlaps and related; the source is gift_xrefs.tsv. The namespace is open so that resources beyond KEGG can be linked.
effect: No change to any GIFT call. get_gift_pathways() and gifts_for_pathway() read the links, and the atlas shows them on each GIFT. Fourteen GIFTs are linked to KEGG modules and pathway maps; MetaCyc identifiers are accepted by the schema but not yet curated.

summary: Reactions carry a stable reaction_id and an optional Rhea master
rationale: Rhea coverage of polymer-acting chemistry is incomplete because a polysaccharide is a substrate class rather than a compound with a balanced equation. Requiring a Rhea master as reaction identity would have excluded most carbohydrate-active chemistry from the database. Rhea remains preferred and remains the reaction_id wherever it exists; a reaction without one must instead carry at least one cross-reference.
evidence: CAZy family and characterised-activity records; absence of Rhea master reactions for endo-acting glycoside hydrolases on polymeric substrates.
effect: No change to any existing GIFT call. reaction_id equals the Rhea master for all reactions curated so far.

summary: Anchors carry a molecule key and a two-state compartment qualifier
rationale: Depolymerisation, uptake and intracellular saccharification are separate ecological strategies, and distinguishing them requires saying which side of the membrane a boundary molecule sits on. Compartment is a curated boundary claim, not a genomic inference: markers identify chemistry, not localisation. The qualifier is limited to declared anchors; no other part of gifter is compartmentalised.
evidence: Curation proposal inst/doc/proposal-polysaccharide-degradation.md sections 4 and 8.2; selfish versus public-goods glycan foraging literature.
effect: No change to any existing GIFT call. Every existing anchor is compartment unspecified, and graph edges between unspecified anchors remain exact.

summary: GIFTs declare a mode and composition cycles are checked within a mode
rationale: Catabolism and biosynthesis legitimately close loops through shared metabolites, so the acyclicity check that protects boundary curation would reject correct content once degradation GIFTs are added. Cycles remain forbidden within a mode, which is where they still indicate a boundary error.
evidence: Worked example: GlcNAc degradation to fructose 6-phosphate against amino sugar biosynthesis from fructose 6-phosphate.
effect: No change to any existing GIFT call. All content curated so far is anabolic.

summary: Nine monosaccharide and uronate degradation GIFTs added as the first catabolic content
rationale: Monosaccharide catabolism is the tier that connects carbohydrate degradation to central metabolism, and it is the half of the degradation model that needs no polymer chemistry. Each GIFT ends at the central metabolite the sugar actually becomes, so capabilities that yield different products are separate traits rather than routes of one trait.
evidence: Rhea release 141 master reactions and KEGG orthology, every accession verified against the resource on 2026-08-18. KEGG modules M00632 and M00061 match two of the nine boundaries exactly; the other seven have no module.
effect: Nine new positive calls become possible. No existing GIFT call changes; the new content shares no reaction with the biosynthetic GIFTs.

summary: The bifunctional biosynthetic enzyme GNE is not accepted as evidence for N-acetylmannosamine kinase
rationale: GNE (K12409) carries a N-acetylmannosamine kinase domain and so catalyses the curated chemistry, but in the organisms that encode it that activity belongs to sialic acid biosynthesis rather than catabolism. Accepting it would call sialic acid degradation in genomes that only synthesise it, destroying the distinction the GIFT exists to draw.
evidence: KEGG orthology entry K12409, annotated as bifunctional UDP-N-acetylglucosamine 2-epimerase / N-acetylmannosamine kinase.
effect: N-acetylneuraminate degradation is not called from GNE alone. Genomes carrying nanK or the bifunctional nanEK are unaffected.

summary: Aldose 1-epimerase is optional in the Leloir route
rationale: Mutarotation between the alpha and beta anomers of D-galactose also proceeds spontaneously, so a genome lacking aldose 1-epimerase still runs the Leloir pathway. The reaction is retained at required = 0 so that it appears in the evidence trace without gating the call.
evidence: Spontaneous anomerisation of reducing sugars in aqueous solution; KEGG M00632 includes galM but the pathway operates without it.
effect: Galactose degradation is called in genomes carrying galK, galT and galE but no recognised aldose 1-epimerase.

summary: D-xylose and L-arabinose uptake curated, and their anchors split by compartment
rationale: Import is what separates a genome that can use a sugar released by others from one that merely encodes the catabolic enzymes, and it is the first place the compartment layer carries real content. Both pentoses have substrate-specific ABC importer orthologues and a Rhea master for the translocation, so both conditions of the splitting licence are met.
evidence: KEGG orthology K10543/K10544/K10545, K10537/K10538/K10539 and K25045/K25046/K25047; Rhea master reactions RHEA:29899 and RHEA:30007, both carrying explicit (out) and (in) participants.
effect: Two new positive calls become possible, and the first composition edges in the catabolic half of the database appear: uptake now feeds the matching degradation GIFT through the cytoplasmic anchor.

summary: Uptake GIFTs are curated only where transporter markers are substrate-specific and the translocation has a verified reaction identity
rationale: Fucose, galactose and mannose are moved mainly by promiscuous carriers: the KEGG orthologue for fucose uptake is annotated as a fucose-galactose-glucose symporter, so accepting it would attribute fucose uptake to any genome carrying that family. Sialic acid, hexuronate and N-acetylglucosamine have substrate-specific markers but no reaction identity gifter can verify, because their symporters and importers carry no EC number and no Rhea master. In both cases no uptake GIFT is curated and the substrate anchor stays compartment-unspecified, so no catabolic chain is broken by a transporter that could not be evidenced.
evidence: KEGG orthology entry K02429, annotated as an MFS fucose-galactose-glucose:H+ symporter; absence of an EC number or Rhea master for K03290 (nanT), K08191 (exuT) and K10200/K10201/K10202 (ngcEFG).
effect: No call changes. Seven substrates keep an unspecified anchor and remain callable from their catabolic markers alone.

summary: The pentose anchors use the generic sugar rather than a single anomer
rationale: Rhea represents ABC import of the generic sugar and uses one ChEBI identifier for both sides of the membrane. The anomer-specific identities previously recorded described the isomerase substrate rather than the boundary molecule, and would have made the transport and catabolic reactions appear to act on different substances.
evidence: Rhea RHEA:29899 and RHEA:30007 use CHEBI:53455 and CHEBI:17535 for both the external and internal participant.
effect: No call changes; no route reaction was altered.

summary: Arabinoxylan and starch depolymerisation and saccharification curated as separate tiers
rationale: Endo-acting depolymerisation and exo-acting saccharification are curated as separate GIFTs because possessing one without the other is the primary-degrader versus cross-feeder distinction, which is the main thing a carbohydrate database is asked to resolve. Polymer and oligosaccharide anchors are extracellular: a polymer cannot cross a membrane, and no oligosaccharide importer could be evidenced, so the products of their cleavage are outside the cell. Side-chain release earns its own GIFT because the released L-arabinose is itself an anchored fermentable sugar.
evidence: CAZy family and activity assignments from dbCAN db_v5-2-9_5-5-2026 fam-substrate-mapping.tsv; KEGG orthology entries verified 2026-08-18. None of the six EC numbers has a Rhea master reaction.
effect: Six new positive calls become possible, and the first complete traversal from a dietary polysaccharide to central metabolism appears in the derived graph.

summary: CAZy families accepted as markers, with confidence derived from measured family polyspecificity
rationale: A CAZy family is a sequence family, not an activity. Accepting a family as evidence for one of its activities silently attributes the others, so confidence is set from the number of distinct characterised activities the family carries in dbCAN: one activity is curated, two or three is high-confidence, four or more is ambiguous. GH5 carries 28 and GH13 carries 34, so neither is evidence for a specific chemistry on its own; GH52, GH120 and GH62 carry one each.
evidence: Distinct EC counts computed directly from the pinned dbCAN mapping and recorded per marker in component_markers.notes.
effect: Calls resting only on polyspecific families report evidence_confidence = ambiguous rather than reading like curated orthology.

summary: A CAZy family and a KEGG orthologue are alternative markers of one catalytic role, not alternative enzyme systems
rationale: The proposal suggested one enzyme system per non-homologous CAZy family. At implementation these are all single-protein hydrolases, and an annotation pipeline cannot tell whether the family hit and the orthology hit describe the same protein - they usually do. Modelling them as alternative systems would imply two enzymes where there is one. The system and component layers remain available for genuinely multi-subunit CAZyme architectures.
evidence: Absence of subunit structure in the curated hydrolases; overlap between CAZy and KEGG annotation of the same protein.
effect: No call changes; the Boolean result is identical either way.

summary: Polysaccharide degradation is curated per substrate capability rather than per enzymatic step
rationale: The first polysaccharide release split each substrate into single-reaction GIFTs for endo-acting depolymerisation, exo-acting saccharification and debranching. That made a GIFT equivalent to a reaction, which is the marker-checklist shape the ontology exists to avoid, and it left the question a user actually asks - can this genome degrade xylan - unanswerable by any single trait. The separation was motivated by the primary-degrader versus cross-feeder distinction, which is real, but that distinction is already carried by the incomplete-route diagnostics: a genome with only the endo-acting enzyme is now reported as incomplete with the exo-acting reaction named as missing, which is more informative than a separate positive trait because it says what is absent. Oligosaccharide intermediates return to being internal; they would be promoted back to anchors only if an oligosaccharide importer could be evidenced, which would make selfish foraging an independently meaningful capability.
evidence: gifter evaluation contract: route completeness with closest-route and missing-reaction reporting. Invariant 9 of AGENTS.md, which forbids both arbitrary single-step fragments and bundles of independently meaningful capabilities.
effect: Six single-reaction GIFTs are replaced by three substrate-level capabilities. Genomes carrying a complete endo-plus-exo enzyme set keep a positive call; genomes carrying only one side of it now report an incomplete capability with the missing reaction named, where they previously reported a positive call for a fragment. Two anchors are withdrawn.

summary: The curator note for polymer saccharification no longer claims that the exo-acting enzyme cannot release a monosaccharide on its own
rationale: The note justified requiring both activities by asserting that neither alone liberates a usable monosaccharide. The second half of that is chemically wrong. EC 3.2.1.37 is defined by IUBMB as xylan 1,4-beta-xylosidase, removing successive D-xylose residues from the non-reducing termini of xylans, so it can release D-xylose from the polymer directly; the same applies to EC 3.2.1.20 on alpha-glucan termini. The reason both reactions are required is a curation decision about what counts as evidence for effective polymer-to-monosaccharide saccharification, not a claim about what either enzyme can catalyse. Endo-acting cleavage generates the additional chain ends that make exo-acting release productive on a polymer rather than marginal.
evidence: IUBMB enzyme nomenclature for EC 3.2.1.37 and EC 3.2.1.20; the curated reaction description of RXN_XYLOOLIGO_EXO already stated the correct substrate.
effect: No call changes and no route changes. The requirement is unaltered; only its stated justification is corrected.

summary: CAZy subfamily markers curated from the dbCAN-sub HMM library, with confidence from measured EC dominance
rationale: Marker policy prefers a subfamily over a polyspecific family, but the family-level substrate mapping shipped by dbCAN contains no subfamily rows, so the first polysaccharide release accepted bare families and recorded them as ambiguous. The subfamily assignments live in the dbCAN-sub HMM library, whose profile names encode the eCAMI cluster, its parent family, the official CAZy subfamilies it contains, and the EC numbers its members carry, each with a member count. Streaming the library and keeping only those names yields a 104 KB table from a 4.9 GB artifact. Confidence now comes from two measured quantities rather than one: how dominant an EC is among the EC-annotated members of a cluster, and how many members support it. Clusters whose parent family belongs to a different catalytic class are excluded, and carbohydrate-binding modules are excluded entirely because they catalyse nothing.
evidence: dbCAN-sub HMM library db_v5-2-9_5-5-2026, 53411 profiles, of which 2474 carry at least one EC assignment; derived table in data-raw/reference/cazy-subfamily-ec.tsv with the extraction script alongside it.
effect: 267 subfamily evidence rows added across seven catalytic components. Genomes annotated by dbCAN-sub gain calls they previously missed, and a call resting on a specific subfamily now reports curated or high-confidence where a bare family reported ambiguous. Bare families are retained as a lower-confidence fallback, so no genome loses a call.

summary: GIFTs and anchors carry a registered facet vocabulary, and a derived profile is exposed alongside it
rationale: A single free-text category could not answer questions that cut across it, and the information needed to answer them was already present in the declared anchors and the compartment layer with no way out. The facet vocabulary is registered so that a multi-valued classification cannot degenerate into free text: substrate_class is single-valued and therefore partitions the database, while physiological_role and the anchor facets are multi-valued and return supersets. Nothing in the derived profile is curated, and neither facets nor profile enter the completeness logic that produces a call.
evidence: Declared anchors, anchor compartment, and the anchor-derived composition graph, all already present in the database.
effect: No call changes. The former gift.category column is replaced by the substrate_class facet.

summary: Collagen cleavage curated as the first protein-degradation GIFT, with a protein substrate class and a host tissue degradation role
rationale: Protein degradation was proposed as a layer of eight substrate-specific traits. Applying the evidence test of the polysaccharide proposal to real markers licensed one. Collagen passes on mechanism rather than on nomenclature: EC 3.4.24.3 is defined by digestion of native collagen in the triple-helical region, an activity generic endopeptidases lack because the intact helix resists them, and KEGG assigns K01387 to MEROPS family M9 and to extracellular-matrix-damaging toxins while keeping the host collagenases MMP-1 and MMP-8 as separate orthologues. The trait therefore claims no more than its markers support. The product is anchored as collagen peptides rather than as a shared peptide pool, because a pool has no membership criterion and would connect every protein-degradation GIFT to every other one's downstream through an undefined intermediate; a shared oligopeptide tier is deferred behind peptide transporter evidence, on the same licence that keeps oligosaccharides internal. The capability needed no schema change: anchors were never restricted to small molecules, rhea_master has been nullable since schema 4, and the marker namespace vocabulary is open.
evidence: KEGG orthology K01387 and EC 3.4.24.3, verified 2026-08-18; Pfam PF01752 via InterPro, retrieved 2026-08-18; Rhea searched 2026-08-18 and found to contain collagen hydroxylation, glycosylation and crosslinking but no proteolytic cleavage of the helix. Full assessment in inst/doc/proposal-protein-degradation.md.
effect: One GIFT, two anchors, one reaction, one route, one enzyme system, one component and two marker evidence rows are added. Genomes encoding a family M9 collagenase gain a positive call. Four facet terms are registered and two anchor facet definitions are broadened from glycan-only wording to cover proteins; no existing anchor is reclassified and no existing call changes.

summary: Trait specificity may not exceed marker specificity, and seven candidate protein-degradation traits are refused under that rule
rationale: The rule was already enforced for carbohydrate-active enzymes as marker policy, where accepting a polyspecific family such as GH5 for a cellulose component would make every mannan degrader a cellulose degrader. Stated as marker policy it reads as advice about confidence values; it is in fact a constraint on what a GIFT may be called, so it is promoted to a named invariant. The protein layer makes the constraint concrete. Elastin cleavage was refused although a named orthologue exists, because EC 3.4.24.26 defines pseudolysin as hydrolysing elastin, collagen types III and IV, fibronectin and immunoglobulin A: accepting it would attribute an elastin-specific claim to a broadly proteolytic enzyme, and would equally license a collagen call, silently equating the two traits. That is the first recorded case of an over-broad marker damaging a trait other than the one it was accepted for. Keratin cleavage was refused for want of any orthologue, keratinolysis being an assay phenotype of subtilisins rather than a clade. Albumin, actin, glutelin, tropomyosin and troponin cleavage were refused because no microbial protease orthologue exists for them; searching for those substrates returns the host structural proteins themselves.
evidence: KEGG orthology and enzyme records searched 2026-08-18 for each candidate substrate. Reasoning and per-substrate outcomes in inst/doc/proposal-protein-degradation.md, section 4.
effect: No call changes. Seven candidate traits are refused rather than deferred silently, so the reasons are available when the evidence changes. AGENTS.md gains invariant 16.

summary: GIFT becomes an umbrella concept with an explicit gift_type
rationale: A genome encodes capabilities that are not chemistry. Modelling a flagellum or a restriction-modification system as a directed route between molecular anchors would have required inventing input and output molecules that the structure does not have, and the resulting call would rest on a boundary claim nobody could defend. Making the kind of capability explicit lets each type state its own completeness contract instead.
evidence: Reviewed against the existing metabolic model: every curated GIFT to date is a claim about chemistry between declared anchors, and none of the four non-metabolic capability types examined (structural, regulatory, defense, developmental) can be stated that way without fabricated anchors.
effect: All 29 existing GIFTs became gift_type = metabolic with no change to their anchors, routes, reactions, systems, components, markers, calls or traces. The anchor/route model, the composition graph and the derived profile are now metabolic-only by construction.

summary: Flagellar apparatus added as the first structural GIFT
rationale: The flagellum is the clearest case of a capability whose completeness is architectural rather than chemical: it is complete when a curated set of structural and assembly functions is jointly supported, and it has no meaningful input or output molecule. It exercises alternative architectures, multisubunit systems, a fused protein serving two components, and the evidence-specificity limit on ion coupling.
evidence: KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18. Structural decomposition follows the export gate, basal body, C ring, hook, hook-filament junction, filament and stator of the characterised enterobacterial and Bacillus flagella; the L and P rings are curated as a separate diderm architecture because monoderms build a flagellum without them.
effect: flagellar_apparatus becomes callable through two architectures, ARCH_FLAGELLUM_DIDERM and ARCH_FLAGELLUM_MONODERM, sharing nine structural functions. No metabolic call changed.

summary: Proton- and sodium-driven flagellar apparatus refused at KO evidence level
rationale: Naming a GIFT for its coupling ion would claim a specificity the evidence does not carry. The specificity of a GIFT claim must not exceed the specificity of the genomic evidence supporting it, and this is the structural instance of that invariant.
evidence: KEGG assigns Vibrio cholerae PomA (VC_0892) and PomB (VC_0893), the sodium-driven polar flagellar stator, to K02556 and K02557, the same orthologues as the proton-driven MotA and MotB of Escherichia coli. MotX (K21217) and MotY (K21218) are specific to the sodium-type polar T ring but evidence a scaffold rather than an ion channel, and are absent from the sodium-driven MotPS motors of alkaliphilic Bacillus.
effect: proton_driven_flagellar_apparatus and sodium_driven_flagellar_apparatus were not curated. The single flagellar_apparatus GIFT is deliberately silent about coupling ion, and the refusal is recorded in inst/doc/proposal-structural-gifts.md.

summary: Type IVa pilus machinery added as a second structural GIFT
rationale: A second structural capability with a substantially different architecture from the flagellum was needed to show that the structural model is not a flagellum-shaped special case. It also carries the accessory-function case: a pilus can be assembled by a genome that cannot retract it.
evidence: KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18. Scoped to the type IVa system because the PilM/N/O/P alignment subcomplex markers are specific to it.
effect: type_iva_pilus becomes callable through ARCH_T4AP_CORE with six required functions and retraction curated as accessory. The claim is deliberately confined to encoding the assembly machinery and does not extend to twitching motility, natural competence or adhesion.

summary: Core chemotaxis signal transduction added as the first regulatory GIFT
rationale: The chemotaxis pathway is the clearest case of a capability that is neither chemistry nor a structure: it is an information-transduction circuit, complete when a receptor, a kinase core, a response regulator and an adaptation cycle are jointly encoded. It was curated first because it needs no evidence the marker model lacks.
evidence: KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18: K03406, K03407, K03408, K00575, K03412, K03413 and the termination phosphatases K03414, K03410, K03409. Receptor distribution was measured rather than assumed: Escherichia coli K-12 carries no K03406 orthologue, its four receptors being assigned to the characterised groups K05874, K05875, K05876 and K03776, while Pseudomonas aeruginosa carries 21 K03406 genes and Vibrio cholerae 34.
effect: chemotaxis_signal_transduction becomes callable through CIRCUIT_CHEMOTAXIS_CORE with four required functions. The reception function accepts a generic or a characterised chemoreceptor, so an Escherichia coli annotation is not called receptor-less. Signal termination is accessory with three non-homologous systems.

summary: Ligand-specific chemoreception curated as a separate claim with separate evidence
rationale: Regulatory specificity cannot exceed evidence specificity. A generic methyl-accepting chemotaxis protein identifies the conserved cytoplasmic signalling domain shared by every chemoreceptor and says nothing about the periplasmic domain that determines what is detected. Rather than leave the principle implicit, a narrower claim was curated with strictly narrower evidence.
evidence: K03406 is assigned to 34 genes in Vibrio cholerae and 21 in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, so it cannot single out any one chemoeffector. K05875 is the Tar orthologue group, anchored on the characterised aspartate and maltose sensor of Escherichia coli and Salmonella.
effect: aspartate_chemoreception requires K05875 for its reception function and refuses K03406. A genome carrying only a generic chemoreceptor completes chemotaxis_signal_transduction and not aspartate_chemoreception, which is the intended behaviour.

summary: Phosphate starvation response added with two cognate-pair circuits
rationale: The regulatory proposal recorded orthology calibration as the question blocking this trait: whether K07636 and K07657 distinguish a cognate Pho pair from a genome full of paralogous kinases and regulators. The calibration was done and the answer separated one capability into two circuits sharing a sensor.
evidence: Gene counts per genome from the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18. K07636 is single-copy in Escherichia coli, Bacillus subtilis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Salmonella Typhi and Vibrio cholerae, and absent from Campylobacter jejuni, Helicobacter pylori, Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Lactococcus lactis. K07657 is single-copy in the four Gram-negatives and absent from Bacillus subtilis, which instead carries K07658 at BSU29110, immediately adjacent to the K07636 sensor BSU29100. The two regulator groups are mutually exclusive across the genomes checked.
effect: phosphate_starvation_response becomes callable through CIRCUIT_PHO_PHOR_PHOB and CIRCUIT_PHO_PHOR_PHOP, which share the RF_PHO_SIGNAL_RECEPTION function. K07660, the response regulator of the magnesium-sensing PhoP/PhoQ system, is refused despite sharing the gene name. PstSCAB-PhoU is accessory.

summary: Type I restriction-modification added as the first defense GIFT
rationale: A defense capability is not the sum of its convenient parts. Type I restriction-modification was curated first because it makes that explicit: the mechanism is complete only when recognition, host protection and restriction are all encoded, and the multisubunit requirement is real rather than a modelling choice.
evidence: KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18. K01153, K03427 and K01154 are defined as the R, M and S subunits of a type I restriction enzyme, so the accessions separate type I from types II, III and IV. Escherichia coli K-12 carries one of each, the EcoKI system.
effect: type_i_restriction_modification becomes callable through MECH_TYPE_I_RM with three required functions. A genome carrying only HsdM and HsdS is called incomplete, missing DF_TYPE_I_RM_RESTRICTION. The target sequence recognised by HsdS is not claimed, because the variable target recognition domains are not resolved by the orthology group.

summary: Type I-E CRISPR-Cas curated as an encoded-machinery claim, not an interference claim
rationale: A CRISPR-Cas system without a CRISPR array has no guide RNAs and interferes with nothing, and an array is a repeat-spacer locus detected by structure rather than a protein annotation. gifter's evidence layer is a namespaced accession and cannot express it. Rather than pretend protein markers cover the array, or refuse the trait entirely, the claim was narrowed to what the evidence supports.
evidence: KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18: K19123, K19046, K19124, K19125 and K19126 are defined as Cascade subunits CasA, CasB, CasC, CasD and CasE, and K07012 as the Cas3 endonuclease-helicase. Escherichia coli K-12 carries one of each plus K15342 and K09951.
effect: type_i_e_crispr_cas_machinery becomes callable through MECH_TYPE_I_E_CRISPR with Cascade and Cas3 required and Cas1-Cas2 adaptation accessory. The array limitation is stated in the GIFT description rather than a footnote. K07475, the HD module of a split Cas3, is refused as evidence of the complete nuclease-helicase. Extending the evidence model to genomic features is deferred to a second demonstrated need.

summary: Short-chain fatty acid formation curated as five GIFTs, with a sixth connecting them to existing catabolic content
rationale: gifter's catabolic layer ended at pyruvate and the deoxyhexose GIFTs ended at (S)-lactaldehyde, so the fermentation products those routes exist to explain could not be called. acetate_interconversion, butyrate_formation, propionate_formation_propanediol and propionate_formation_acrylate name the products; pyruvate_to_acetyl_coa and propanediol_formation connect them to what is already curated, so that no SCFA GIFT is an isolated node in the composition graph.
evidence: KEGG module M00579 for the acetate node; KEGG orthology-to-gene links retrieved 2026-08-18 over 11856 organisms for prevalence and co-occurrence; Rhea release 141 for all eighteen reactions; ChEBI release 253 for the six new anchors; NCBIfam TIGR03948 and InterPro IPR023990 for the butyrate terminal step; KEGG reaction records for the cross-references. Full assessment in inst/doc/proposal-scfa-biosynthesis.md.
effect: Six GIFTs become callable. pyruvate_to_acetyl_coa composes with galacturonate and glucuronate degradation through PYRUVATE; propanediol_formation composes with fucose and rhamnose degradation through LACTALDEHYDE; acetate_interconversion composes into butyrate_formation through ACETATE. No existing GIFT call changes, because no existing route, system, component or marker was edited.

summary: The butyrate terminal step is evidenced by NCBIfam TIGR03948, the first non-KO, non-CAZy marker in the metabolic layer
rationale: KEGG orthology cannot express this trait. K01034 and K01035 carry EC 2.8.3.8 and EC 2.8.3.9 together, so the accession that would stand for butyryl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase is the same one that stands for the acetoacetate degradation transferase of Escherichia coli. Accepting it would have equated butyrate formation with acetoacetate catabolism, which is the damage the evidence-specificity invariant describes.
evidence: Of 39 KEGG genomes in canonical butyrate-producing genera, 31 complete the KO core and 9 carry any terminal KO; Faecalibacterium prausnitzii L2-6, Agathobacter rectalis ATCC 33656 and Roseburia intestinalis XB6B4 carry none, while Bacillus subtilis 168 carries both terminal KO sets. Of 366 organisms completing the KO core with phosphate butyryltransferase and butyrate kinase, 120 are Bacillus and 16 Geobacillus. TIGR03948 matches 178 proteins in 171 proteomes, led by Faecalibacterium, Roseburia, Eubacterium and Anaerostipes, and matches no Bacillus, Escherichia, Salmonella or Pseudomonas.
effect: butyrate_formation is callable at the specificity its name claims. Users supplying TIGRFAM accessions already had them recognised by the evaluator; this is the first curated row that uses one. No other GIFT is affected.

summary: The butyrate kinase route is refused and the refusal recorded
rationale: Phosphate butyryltransferase and butyrate kinase are not specific to butyrate formation. They serve branched-chain acyl-CoA metabolism in aerobic Bacillota, and the non-specificity is a property of the enzymes rather than of KEGG's annotation, so no change of marker namespace repairs it.
evidence: K00634 with K00929 is complete in 817 KEGG organisms and in 366 that also complete the acetyl-CoA core, of which 120 are Bacillus. At sequence-family level the picture is the same: NCBIfam TIGR02707 matches 2279 proteins with Bacillus the second most frequent genus, and TIGR02706 matches 573 with Bacillus second after Clostridium.
effect: butyrate_formation carries one route rather than two. A genome whose only butyrate-releasing enzyme is Buk is called negative, which is the honest answer at this evidence level. Revisit if a marker separates fermentative Ptb/Buk from the branched-chain acyl-CoA enzymes.

summary: The succinate (Wood-Werkman) route to propionate is refused and the refusal recorded
rationale: Its markers are direction-blind and taxonomically misleading. Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and the methylmalonyl-CoA decarboxylase are the same genes KEGG module M00741 uses to degrade propanoyl-CoA, so the same evidence supports the opposite claim, and the CoA-transferase releasing propionate is not resolved by any orthology group in the organisms that matter most.
evidence: Mutase with decarboxylase and a candidate CoA-transferase is complete in 177 KEGG organisms, or 293 if the methylmalonyl-CoA carboxyltransferase K17489 is also accepted; the leading genera of that set are Corynebacterium (70), Escherichia (19), Cutibacterium (16) and Klebsiella (13). Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, the dominant gut propionate producer, is negative because it carries no transferase KO, and its K00634 with K00929 pair is the same one already refused for butyrate.
effect: Propionate is callable through the propanediol and acrylate routes only. Genomes producing propionate through succinate are called negative. Revisit when a marker resolves propionate release and separates the biosynthetic from the degradative direction.

summary: acetate_interconversion is declared mode = interconversion and declares both of its boundaries in both roles, the first use of that mode value
rationale: The phosphotransacetylase and acetate kinase node is near-equilibrium and physiologically bidirectional, so naming it a formation and declaring only ACETYL_COA to ACETATE would assert a direction the markers do not evidence. Splitting it into a formation GIFT and an assimilation GIFT would assert a distinction the same two genes cannot make either, so the one GIFT declares both directions. The mode also keeps any future acetate-activation GIFT out of a within-mode cycle with this one.
evidence: KEGG module M00579 records the acetyl-CoA to acetate direction only; the same two enzymes run towards acetyl-CoA in acetate-assimilating genomes such as Escherichia coli at high acetate, and no marker distinguishes the directions. 6582 of 11856 KEGG organisms carry the pair.
effect: The GIFT was renamed from acetate_formation, because formation names a direction its own description says the evidence cannot establish. The mode CHECK branch that had never been exercised now carries content and a stated contract. Composition from this node into butyrate_formation runs through both ACETATE and ACETYL_COA; both edges cross a mode boundary and are therefore exempt from the catabolic cycle scan, which is the intended behaviour.

summary: The electron-transfer flavoprotein is not a required component of the butanoyl-CoA dehydrogenase system
rationale: K03521 and K03522 are the generic fixA and fixB orthologues shared with nitrogen fixation. A marker present in almost every genome carries no evidence about butyrate, so requiring it would trade recall for no gain in specificity. The route's specificity comes from its terminal transferase, not from the electron carrier.
evidence: K03521 and K03522 together are present in 7729 of 11856 KEGG organisms. Among the 39 genomes in canonical butyrate-producing genera, 31 complete the acetyl-CoA core but only 20 carry both flavoprotein subunits; Faecalibacterium prausnitzii L2-6 carries K03522 and no K03521.
effect: butyrate_formation is complete in genomes whose flavoprotein subunits are unannotated. The biological reading is unchanged: the complex needs the flavoprotein, and gifter is stating that it does not use it as evidence.

summary: The interconversion mode gains a boundary contract the source validator enforces
rationale: The mode value existed in the schema CHECK with nothing behind it and no stated meaning, which is the situation AGENTS.md forbids for a type and which is no better for a mode. Curating the first interconversion GIFT is the point at which the contract has to be written down, because the alternative is a mode whose meaning is inferred from one example.
evidence: Declaring a reversible node in one direction asserts a direction the markers do not support; declaring it in both required relaxing the rule that no anchor may carry both roles. That rule was doing real work: two compartments of one molecule is the signature of transport, and losing it would stop transport being required to reach the cytoplasm. Separating the two cases by compartment identity keeps that guarantee and adds the new one.
effect: Every anchor of an interconversion GIFT must be declared as both input and output, and no other mode may declare an anchor that way. A molecule appearing in two compartments remains the signature of transport and is no longer conflated with a mirrored boundary. Enforced in R/database-build.R and covered by four fixtures in test-compartment.R. The SQL schema is unchanged at version 6: this is a source-contract rule, not a DDL change.

summary: Organic acid and neutral fermentation product formation curated as six GIFTs, and the citric acid cycle refused as a source of anchors
rationale: The request was to express the capacity to form fumarate, succinate, citrate and lactate. Those four are not one class and the assessment splits them. Lactate, ethanol and acetoin are fermentation end products, which a genome can be said to release and for which a directional marker exists. Citrate, fumarate and succinate are citric acid cycle intermediates, consumed by the pathway that makes them, present in every genome that has the cycle, and with no direction their markers can evidence. Malate and citrate enter as input-only boundaries of capabilities that consume them; nothing in the layer claims to produce them.
evidence: 59 KEGG orthology groups over the 11855 organisms carrying at least one of them, Rhea release 141 for all nine reactions, ChEBI release 253 for the five anchors. Full evidence test in inst/doc/proposal-organic-acid-formation.md.
effect: Six new GIFTs, five new anchors, nine new reactions and twelve new KO markers. The substrate_class vocabulary gains organic_acid and neutral_fermentation_product, and physiological_role fermentative_end_product is broadened from short-chain fatty acids to fermentation end products generally. propionate_formation_acrylate stops being an orphan at its input.

summary: lactate_formation is the first fermentation end product whose direction is evidenced rather than asserted
rationale: The SCFA layer had to declare acetate an interconversion because the same phosphotransacetylase and acetate kinase run the node in both directions and no marker separates them. Lactate is different, and the reason is chemical: forming lactate is a cytoplasmic NADH-consuming reduction, while consuming it feeds electrons to a quinone or a cytochrome. Those are different enzymes with different cofactors and KEGG gives them different orthology groups, so the catabolic declaration is supported by the marker rather than added on top of it.
evidence: K00016 in 4143 organisms and the quinone-dependent K29125 in 3388, sharing only 573. Lactococcus lactis, Lactobacillus delbrueckii, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, Streptococcus pyogenes, Enterococcus faecalis, Bifidobacterium longum and Bacillus subtilis carry the forming group and not the consuming one; Escherichia coli, Salmonella Typhimurium and Pseudomonas aeruginosa are the reverse.
effect: K29125, K00101, K03777 and K00102 are recorded as refused markers rather than accepted alternatives. The GIFT is declared catabolic, not interconversion.

summary: Citric acid cycle intermediates are refused as output anchors, and succinate, fumarate and citrate formation are refused as traits
rationale: Three independent reasons, checked rather than argued. First, the markers carry no information: citrate synthase is in 8467 of 11855 organisms and adenylosuccinate lyase, which releases fumarate and which gifter already curates inside purine_core_biosynthesis and adenylate_biosynthesis, is in 11115. Second, they carry no direction: KEGG names the group that would have to evidence succinate formation sdhA, frdA, and requiring the narrow frdABCD instead calls Vibrio, Escherichia and Klebsiella positive while calling Bacteroides, Prevotella and Fibrobacter negative. Third, the cycle is a cycle: six catabolic GIFTs spanning citrate to oxaloacetate close a within-mode loop in anchor-derived composition and the build fails. There is no boundary to demote, because no acid in the cycle is only ever consumed.
evidence: Running the validator's own edge derivation and .find_graph_cycle() over the current gift_anchors.tsv plus the hypothetical rows reports the catabolic cycle, and reports that declaring FUMARATE on the GIFTs whose curated reactions already involve it adds two edges from purine to pyrimidine biosynthesis that mean nothing.
effect: No SUCCINATE, FUMARATE, OXALOACETATE or 2-oxoglutarate anchor exists. MALATE and CITRATE exist as input-only anchors of capabilities that consume them, and oxaloacetate stays an internal intermediate of the citrate route. A metabolite does not need an anchor to be modelled.

summary: Formate formation is refused on the per-GIFT anchor rule rather than on evidence
rationale: Pyruvate formate-lyase with its activase is complete in 2843 organisms and the reaction is effectively irreversible towards formate, so the evidence is not the obstruction. gift_anchor is keyed on gift, role and ordinal, so anchors are declared per GIFT and not per route, and the lyase is one of three routes of pyruvate_to_acetyl_coa. Declaring FORMATE an output would claim that the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex and pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase produce it too. Curating a separate formate GIFT over the same reaction would duplicate a curated route.
evidence: KEGG K00656 with K04069 in 2843 organisms; the three curated routes of pyruvate_to_acetyl_coa are PYR_ACOA_PDH, PYR_ACOA_PFOR and PYR_ACOA_PFL.
effect: No FORMATE anchor and no formate GIFT. The trigger for revisiting is per-route boundary anchors, or a deliberate decision to split the lyase route out of pyruvate_to_acetyl_coa into its own GIFT.

summary: D-lactate formation is deferred, and the (R)-lactate anchor is reached through the racemase instead
rationale: K03778 is specific to the right chemistry but its leading genera are Pseudomonas, Streptomyces and Burkholderia, obligate aerobes running the NAD-dependent reaction oxidatively, so it fails the direction clause without acetate's justification for accepting that failure. The organisms that actually need (R)-lactate mostly do not have it: of the ten KEGG genomes behind propionate_formation_acrylate, eight carry lactate racemase and only two carry K03778.
evidence: K03778 in 3133 organisms led by Pseudomonas (224), Streptomyces (158) and Burkholderia (90). Megasphaera elsdenii, M. stantonii, M. massiliensis, M. hexanoica, Pseudocoprococcus catus and three Desulfosporosinus carry K22373 and not K03778; the two Anaerotignum genomes are the reverse.
effect: No D-lactate formation GIFT. If one is curated later the honest form is a route whose marker mapping is recorded as ambiguous, so that evidence_confidence reports the weakness at the call.

summary: The acetolactate synthase step of acetoin_formation is curated but not required
rationale: KEGG names K01652 ilvB, ilvG, ilvI: the orthology group that would evidence the condensation step is the anabolic branched-chain amino acid synthase, present in 9341 organisms, and it carries no acetoin-specific information. Acetolactate decarboxylase exists only for this pathway. This is the butyrate decision applied again: evidence the trait on the specific terminal step, not on the shared core.
evidence: K01575 in 1649 organisms led by Streptococcus, Bacillus, Corynebacterium, Staphylococcus, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Listeria, Enterococcus and Lactococcus. Requiring K01652 as well changes the call in 50 of those 1649.
effect: route_reactions.required is 0 for RHEA:25249 and the marker mapping for K01652 is recorded as ambiguous. The chemistry stays curated so that the PYRUVATE boundary is truthful.

summary: Vitamin biosynthesis curated as twenty GIFTs covering B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7, B9, B12 and K2
rationale: The capacity to produce vitamins is the largest capability the ontology could express without a schema change, and the one where the host-relevant claim depends most on where the boundary falls. Each vitamin is cut where genomes measurably differ rather than where the pathway drawing ends: folate at 4-aminobenzoate, thiamine at its two activated moieties, NAD at nicotinate D-ribonucleotide, and cobalamin at the corrin ring, the cobinamide arm and the nucleotide loop.
evidence: KEGG orthology sets for 126 orthology groups intersected over all 10151 bacterial genomes in the KEGG release of 2026-08-18; Rhea release 141, which returned a master reaction for all 100 EC numbers in the layer; ChEBI release 253 for the 31 new anchors; a validation panel of 18 reference genomes spanning Enterobacteriaceae, Bacteroidetes, Clostridia, Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillaceae, Akkermansia and Propionibacterium.
effect: Twenty new callable GIFTs, 31 anchors, 26 routes, 94 reactions and 151 marker assignments. The layer partitions bacteria rather than describing all of them: 1087 of 10151 genomes complete none of the nine vitamin capabilities, 228 complete all nine, and half complete four or fewer. Every GIFT is an auxotrophy indicator in gift_profile, because each declares a biomass-essential output anchor.

summary: Four reactions that no marker identifies at the specificity of the step are curated as not required
rationale: A reaction can be certain chemistry and still have no orthology group that covers it across bacteria. Requiring such a step converts a missing annotation into a false negative for the whole capability, and deleting it makes the route describe chemistry that does not exist. Both are worse than curating the step with required = 0 and recording why.
evidence: Requiring the 5-amino-6-(5-phospho-D-ribitylamino)uracil phosphatase reduces riboflavin biosynthesis from 7943 to 2682 bacterial genomes; requiring the dihydroneopterin triphosphate diphosphatase reduces folate biosynthesis from 5898 to 1634; requiring MenH and the 1,4-dihydroxy-2-naphthoyl-CoA hydrolase reduces the classical menaquinone route from 3109 to 1355.
effect: The four steps remain visible in trace_gift() and in the route tables, and are excluded from completeness. Riboflavin, folate and menaquinone calls are broader than a strict reading of the KEGG modules would give.

summary: A single cobalamin biosynthesis trait is refused; corrin ring, cobinamide arm and nucleotide loop are curated as three capabilities
rationale: Most of the prevalence of the cobalamin pathway is salvage rather than synthesis. A single trait would call corrinoid salvagers producers, which is the worst error this layer could make.
evidence: 4139 of 10151 bacterial genomes complete the nucleotide loop and 3044 of those encode no corrin ring at all, Escherichia coli among them. 1017 genomes complete the anaerobic ring route and 340 the aerobic one.
effect: A genome that imports cobinamide and attaches a lower ligand completes cobamide_nucleotide_loop_assembly and not corrin_ring_biosynthesis. No GIFT in the database claims cobalamin production on the strength of the loop alone.

summary: The lower ligand is curated as its own capability, because a cobamide without dimethylbenzimidazole is not vitamin B12
rationale: The nucleotide loop attaches whichever benzimidazole, purine or phenolic ligand the genome can supply, and only 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole makes the product the vitamin a host can use. Naming the loop after cobalamin would assert a lower ligand the evidence does not establish.
evidence: Of the 1081 bacterial genomes completing ring, cobinamide arm and nucleotide loop, 538 also carry BluB. Limosilactobacillus reuteri completes the corrinoid path and carries no BluB, consistent with its reported production of a cobamide rather than of cobalamin. The anaerobic bza route to the ligand has no KEGG orthology group and is not curated, so a negative dmb_biosynthesis_aerobic call is not evidence that the genome cannot make the ligand.
effect: dmb_biosynthesis_aerobic is callable separately and composes into cobamide_nucleotide_loop_assembly through the DMB anchor.

summary: A cofactor may be declared an anchor only where the reaction consumes it, and cofactor activation steps are not curated
rationale: This layer produces cofactors, so it needs a sharper form of the standing rule against cofactor anchors. Without it, tetrahydrofolate, pyridoxal 5-phosphate and NAD would become input anchors of half the database and the anabolic composition graph would stop describing biosynthesis and start describing cofactor dependence.
evidence: BluB destroys FMNH2 to build the benzimidazole ring, so FMNH2 is a substrate and is declared as an input-only anchor. By contrast the flavin kinase and FMN adenylyltransferase step is complete in all 18 reference genomes, including the six that cannot make riboflavin, so it partitions nothing and tracks annotation rather than biology.
effect: Riboflavin to FAD, pantothenate to coenzyme A, thiamine phosphate to the diphosphate and folate polyglutamylation are not curated. The vitamin, not the working cofactor form, is the output boundary of every GIFT in the layer.

summary: A generic alkaline phosphatase is refused as evidence of the folate dihydroneopterin monophosphatase step, and the step is left uncurated
rationale: The specificity of a claim may not exceed the specificity of its evidence. Accepting alkaline phosphatase here would have fired the step in every genome carrying a phosphatase and would have damaged every other trait that marker also matches.
evidence: K01077 is assigned in 3202 bacterial genomes and K01113 in 2770, in both cases as a general phosphomonoesterase rather than as a folate enzyme.
effect: The folate route runs from the dihydroneopterin triphosphate diphosphatase to the aldolase without a curated monophosphatase reaction, and the route description records the gap.

summary: The ThiS and ThiF sulfur carrier is not a required component of thiazole synthase
rationale: ThiF is homologous to MoeB of molybdopterin biosynthesis and ThiI also serves tRNA thiolation, so neither marker is specific to thiamine. Requiring them would gate the trait on markers that add no thiamine specificity.
evidence: Requiring ThiG together with ThiS and ThiF reduces the thiazole branch from 5396 to 1554 bacterial genomes; Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia and Propionibacterium reference genomes all lack the ThiF assignment while carrying ThiG.
effect: thiazole_phosphate_biosynthesis is complete on thiazole synthase plus an imine-supplying enzyme.

summary: EntC is accepted for the isochorismate synthase reaction of menaquinone biosynthesis
rationale: A marker whose pathway assignment lies elsewhere is still admissible when it is accurate at the level of the reaction. What the specificity rule forbids is a marker whose chemistry is broader than the claim, and EntC catalyses exactly the reaction MenF catalyses. Route completeness supplies the menaquinone specificity.
evidence: Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron annotates BT_4700 as entC and carries no menF; with MenF alone the genome is called menaquinone-negative. Accepting both raises the classical route from 2461 to 4047 genomes carrying the step, and the complete route from 1355 to 3109.
effect: Bacteroidetes genomes that make menaquinone are no longer called negative on the first step.

summary: The corrin ring capability is curated with a known recall limit caused by gene fusion, and no domain marker is accepted to repair it
rationale: Propionibacterium freudenreichii, the organism industrial vitamin B12 comes from, is called incomplete for the corrin ring. Its genome carries the genes, as cysG_cbiX and cobJ_cbiE_cbiG_cbiH fusions that KEGG assigns to none of the component orthology groups. The obvious repair is a domain marker, and it is refused.
evidence: Pfam PF00590 is Tetrapyrrole (Corrin/Porphyrin) Methylases, one family covering CbiE, CbiF, CbiH, CbiL, CobM and diphthine synthase; it cannot say which step a protein performs. PFREUD_07710 and PFREUD_07700 are the two fusions in question.
effect: corrin_ring_biosynthesis reports the closest route with three named missing reactions for that genome rather than a positive call on a widened marker. Precision is preserved at the cost of recall, and the cost is recorded here.

summary: NAD biosynthesis is cut at nicotinate D-ribonucleotide so that de novo synthesis and pyridine salvage share the trunk instead of duplicating it
rationale: Being able to live without niacin and being able to make the pyridine ring are different claims about a genome. Cutting at the mononucleotide lets both exist without either duplicating the adenylyltransferase and synthetase, and avoids a breaking re-cut later.
evidence: 6398 bacterial genomes form quinolinate from aspartate, 6921 recover nicotinate into the trunk, and 6791 carry the trunk itself. The cut follows the precedent set for L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde in the amino acid layer.
effect: Four callable GIFTs share one trunk. A genome positive for namn_salvage_nicotinate and negative for quinolinate_biosynthesis_aspartate is niacin-dependent.

summary: GTP is declared as an input-only anchor and no GIFT is curated to link it to GMP
rationale: The architecture guide already decided this for adenylate: biosynthesis stops at AMP because phosphorylation is shared metabolism. A GMP to GTP capability would assert the opposite for guanylate, and the same gap already exists between the curated UMP output of pyrimidine core biosynthesis and the UTP input of cytidylate biosynthesis.
evidence: Guanylate kinase is assigned in 9625 of 10151 bacterial genomes and nucleoside-diphosphate kinase in 8897, so the trait would be complete in 84 per cent of bacteria while its negatives would be genomes whose Ndk role is filled by another kinase. Ndk is base-generic and adds no guanylate specificity.
effect: riboflavin_biosynthesis and folate_biosynthesis take GTP as an input anchor with no producer GIFT, and gift_graph draws no edge from guanylate_biosynthesis to them.

summary: Cobalamin uptake is refused as a transport GIFT, so the layer reports no cross-feeding output
rationale: The corrinoid importers that matter in host-associated communities are the ones this marker set cannot see. Curating the Proteobacterial system alone would call the dominant gut corrinoid importers negative, which is worse than declining the trait.
evidence: The btuB, btuC and btuD orthology groups are complete together in 734 bacterial genomes, concentrated in Proteobacteria; Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron carries none of the three, and the Bacteroidetes corrinoid receptors have no KEGG orthology group at all.
effect: No anchor in the layer is declared extracellular, so gift_profile reports cross_feeding_output as 0 and resource_strategy as private for all twenty GIFTs. Vitamin sharing remains outside what the model can state.

summary: A co-substrate is not declared as an anchor merely because the reaction consumes it
rationale: The PdxS/PdxT reaction consumes ribose 5-phosphate, glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate and glutamine. Declaring all three would have made every sugar degradation GIFT that ends at glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate an upstream neighbour of vitamin B6 biosynthesis, which says nothing a reader wants: the trait is defined by the pentose and the nitrogen donor, not by the triose.
evidence: Purine core biosynthesis sets the precedent. It declares PRPP and nothing else, although its route also consumes glycine, L-aspartate, formate and glutamine, three of which are curated anchors. Declaring GAP here produced a catabolic-to-anabolic edge from the uronate degradation GIFTs that no reader would have read as biology.
effect: plp_biosynthesis_r5p declares D-ribose 5-phosphate and L-glutamine as inputs. The anchor set of the catabolic layer is unchanged, and its exits remain pyruvate and lactaldehyde.

summary: Oxidative citric acid cycle chemistry curated as four composable segment GIFTs, reversing the earlier finding that the cycle cannot be anchored
rationale: The earlier assessment refused citric acid cycle anchors because it was testing product claims: whether a genome can be said to form and release citrate, fumarate or succinate. Those refusals stand. This layer asks a different question, the one gifter's other GIFTs already answer, which is what chemistry a genome encodes between two boundaries. Segmented that way the cycle is highly informative: all sixteen configurations of the four segments are occupied across 11783 KEGG organisms, and the branched Helicobacter architecture, the actinobacterial decarboxylase bypass and the Bacteroides reductive arm become separable instead of collapsing into one incomplete class. Two of the four segments are declared interconversion rather than directional, because succinate dehydrogenase and fumarate reductase are one orthology group in most bacteria and fumarase and malate dehydrogenase are at equilibrium; claiming a direction there would exceed the evidence.
evidence: 67 KEGG orthology groups over the 11783 organisms carrying at least one of them, retrieved 2026-08-18; Rhea release 141 for all fourteen reactions and every KEGG reaction and EC cross-reference; ChEBI release 253 for the four anchors. Gene-level checks on sau:SA1518, bth:BT_2070, bth:BT_2071 and bth:BT_2072 for the citrate synthase decision. KEGG modules M00009, M00010 and M00011 for the external boundaries. Full assessment in inst/doc/proposal-central-metabolic-cycles.md.
effect: Four new GIFTs, four new anchors, fourteen new reactions and thirty-five new KO markers. A new gift facet, metabolic_cycle, records the curated name of a cycle a GIFT belongs to; whether a genome closes the cycle stays derived. pyruvate_to_acetyl_coa and acetate_interconversion gain outgoing edges through ACETYL_COA, so neither is a terminal node any more. The oxidative citric acid cycle becomes an elementary cycle of the composition graph. No existing GIFT call changes: no existing route, system, component or marker was edited.

summary: Shikimate-derived aromatic biosynthesis curated as three composable GIFTs: chorismate, salicylate and indole-3-acetate
rationale: Chorismate is the point at which aromatic metabolism leaves central carbon metabolism, and gifter already had two GIFTs consuming it and none producing it. Curating the shikimate pathway closes that gap and turns paba_biosynthesis and menaquinone_biosynthesis from entry points into intermediates. Salicylate and indole-3-acetate are curated separately rather than as one aromatic capability, because a GIFT is a directed capability between declared anchors and aromatic compound biosynthesis is a chemical family, not a capability. Indole-3-acetate is cut at tryptophan, not at chorismate: tryptophan is a branchpoint and a building block, and running the trait through aromatic amino acid biosynthesis would bundle two independently useful capabilities.
evidence: Scored across the 10151 bacterial and 470 archaeal genomes of the KEGG release of 2026-08-18. chorismate_biosynthesis completes in 7644 bacteria and 90 archaea; salicylate_biosynthesis in 646 bacteria and no archaeon; indole_3_acetate_biosynthesis in 86 bacteria. 4604 bacteria complete both chorismate and pABA, and 598 both chorismate and salicylate. Ten reactions were added, all with Rhea masters; the salicylate route reuses the existing isochorismate synthase reaction RHEA:18985 rather than duplicating it.
effect: Three new metabolic GIFTs, four new anchors, ten reactions, twenty-three enzyme systems and twenty-one markers. paba_biosynthesis and menaquinone_biosynthesis gain an upstream neighbour in the composition graph and change from network position entry to intermediate.

summary: The shikimate dehydrogenase step of the shikimate pathway is curated as not required
rationale: This is a coverage hole in the marker, not a gap in the biology. Every other step of the pathway is annotated in 8461 to 9149 bacteria while K00014 reaches 5585, and the organisms that fall out are ones that demonstrably make aromatic amino acids.
