It is the orphan-step rule the vitamin layer established, applied to a step that has a KO which does not reach the taxa that need it.
evidence: Requiring the step drops the route from 7644 to 5420 bacteria. The 2224 lost carry every other step and include 201 of 213 Cyanobacteriota and 1061 of 1642 Actinomycetota. Mycobacterium tuberculosis Rv2552c and Synechocystis slr1559 are annotated shikimate 5-dehydrogenase in RefSeq and are assigned to no KO at all. TIGRFAM TIGR00507 was added alongside K00014 so that a genome annotated against NCBIfam satisfies the step; YdiB K05887 was accepted at ambiguous confidence and moves the route by 180 bacteria.
effect: chorismate_biosynthesis completes in 7644 rather than 5420 bacteria. A genome that does carry a shikimate dehydrogenase marker still shows the step as supported in its trace.

summary: PchA and the bifunctional salicylate synthases are curated as enzyme systems of the existing isochorismate synthase reaction, not as a second route to salicylate
rationale: MbtI, Irp9 and YbtS run the same two chemical transformations as PchA and PchB, isomerisation followed by pyruvate elimination, in one active site instead of two proteins. That is a multifunctional protein, which gifter represents at the system layer, exactly as the bifunctional PabBC is curated as a system of both the 4-amino-4-deoxychorismate synthase and lyase reactions. Materialising it as a separate route would assert a different minimal chemical path where there is none.
evidence: KEGG assigns K04781 both EC 5.4.4.2 and EC 4.2.99.21, and the isochorismate intermediate of MbtI is enzyme-bound rather than obligately released. 104 of 109 pchA genomes also carry pchB; 359 bacteria carry K04781; 646 complete the route on some combination.
effect: Enzyme systems attach to reactions rather than to routes, so accepting PchA and MbtI for RHEA:18985 also makes them available to the menaquinone route. That is chemically correct and measurably small: it adds 7 genomes to menaquinone_biosynthesis.

summary: Only the indole-3-acetamide route to the auxin is curated; the indole-3-pyruvate, tryptamine, indole-3-acetonitrile and side-chain oxidase routes are refused
rationale: Every one of the refused routes is real chemistry with no marker that discriminates it. Invariant 16 decides the case: a trait named for indole-3-acetate may not be evidenced by markers that cannot distinguish indole-3-acetate formation from ordinary transamination, decarboxylation or aldehyde oxidation.
evidence: The indole-3-pyruvate route needs an aromatic aminotransferase and an aldehyde dehydrogenase, both generic, plus K04103; KEGG assigns K04103 to proteins annotated only as putative thiamine pyrophosphate enzymes in Salmonella, 417 of its 648 bacterial carriers are Enterobacteria, and one carrier is annotated indolepyruvate/phenylpyruvate decarboxylase. The tryptamine route rests on K01593, which KEGG names aromatic-L-amino-acid/L-tryptophan decarboxylase and which also makes dopamine and serotonin. The nitrile route rests on the broad nitrilase K01501 and has no bacterial marker for the aldoxime step. The side-chain oxidase route has no marker in any namespace.
effect: indole_3_acetate_biosynthesis carries one route and completes in 86 bacteria rather than the several hundred a marker-permissive definition would produce.

summary: Gallate biosynthesis from 3-dehydroshikimate is refused and not curated
rationale: The candidate fails two invariants before the specificity question is even reached. Rhea has no reaction for the dehydrogenation of 3-dehydroshikimate to gallate, so there is no stable reaction identity to curate, and the only enzymes described as performing it are plant shikimate dehydrogenases, whose markers are the AroE markers of the core shikimate pathway. Admitting them would make every genome with a shikimate pathway a gallate producer.
evidence: Rhea release 141 records gallate in nine reactions, all of them consuming it or releasing it from a conjugate, and none forming it from 3-dehydroshikimate. KEGG has eight gallate KOs and every one is degradative or plant-specific: galA/desB dioxygenase, the lpdBCD decarboxylase, ligM, desZ, galR and the plant glucosyltransferase. No EC number, TIGRFAM or Pfam family describes a gallate-forming dehydrogenase.
effect: No GIFT added. The bacterial capability that does have evidence is release of gallate from hydrolysable tannins by tannase, EC 3.1.1.20 and KO K10759, which is different chemistry between different boundaries and is deferred rather than refused.

summary: A biosynthetic_family facet is registered and shikimate_derived_aromatic assigned to five GIFTs
rationale: The four capabilities of this layer share a biosynthetic origin and nothing else that the existing vocabulary records. substrate_class was deliberately not reused: it answers which chemistry a capability is about, and overloading it to mean the chemical family of the product would break the classes it already partitions and could not be assigned to menaquinone or 4-aminobenzoate without taking their cofactor class away.
evidence: The five GIFTs carrying the new value hold three different substrate classes between them, cofactor for 4-aminobenzoate and menaquinone and aromatic_compound for the three new ones, which is the demonstration that the two facets are orthogonal rather than redundant.
effect: Five GIFTs classified. Facets classify a call and never enter the completeness logic, so no genome's result changes.

summary: Fourteen nitrogen, methylamine and organosulfonate catabolism GIFTs curated
rationale: gifter had no nitrogen boundary at all: ammonium appeared in four curated reactions and in no anchor, so every capability that liberates nitrogen was scored only for its carbon. The twelve compounds of distillR bundle D06 were reassessed against KEGG orthology, Rhea 141 and ChEBI 253 over all 10151 bacterial genomes.
evidence: Prevalence computed from KEGG link/genes/ko sets intersected with the 10151 bacterial organism codes of BRITE br08601, KEGG release 2026-08-18. Urea hydrolysis 3725, nitrate assimilation 3045, sarcosine demethylation 2041, taurine ABC uptake 1462, urate degradation 1214, taurine desulfonation 1065, carnitine to betaine 944, allantoin degradation 893, betaine demethylation 759, taurine sulfoacetaldehyde route 397, carnitine to trimethylamine 271, methylamine degradation 213, creatinine degradation 194, ammonium assimilation 9482. The assessment is inst/doc/proposal-nitrogen-compound-catabolism.md.
effect: 5587 of 10151 bacteria complete at least one of the eleven non-transport, non-assimilation capabilities and 4564 complete none. AMMONIUM becomes the most connected anchor in the database, with six incoming GIFTs, and no within-mode cycle arises because nothing in gifter produces urate, allantoin, betaine, creatinine, carnitine, taurine or nitrate.

summary: Ammonium is an anchor only where a reaction exists to liberate or assimilate it
rationale: Ammonium is a common reaction participant, so admitting it as an anchor wherever it appears would make it a boundary of much of the database by accident. The cofactor-anchor rule does not settle this, because it asks whether the molecule is consumed and the ammonia-dependent NAD synthetase genuinely consumes ammonium. The nitrogen rule asks instead what the reaction is for.
evidence: Applied to the four curated reactions that mention NH4(+): RHEA:12172, the glucosamine-6-phosphate deaminase, is admitted because the reaction is the deamination; RHEA:21868 in riboflavin biosynthesis and RHEA:40075 in menaquinone biosynthesis are rejected because ammonium is a leaving group of chemistry aimed at a ring; RHEA:21188, the ammonia-dependent NAD synthetase, is rejected because ammonium is a co-substrate of an amidation.
effect: One admitted, three rejected. Without the rule, riboflavin and menaquinone biosynthesis would become nitrogen sources and NAD biosynthesis would become a nitrogen sink that every ammonium-releasing catabolic GIFT composed into. No call changes.

summary: Capabilities requiring an external terminal electron acceptor are out of scope
rationale: The refusal was already recorded on the FUMARATE anchor for fumarate respiration. The nitrogen layer forces it to become a general rule, because it decides four requested capabilities at once and because the markers for all four are specific, abundant and easy to curate, which is exactly why the boundary needs writing down.
evidence: Refused: nitrate respiration (NarGHI, 2393 bacteria; NapAB, 1326), denitrification (NirK or NirS, 1512), dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (NrfAH, 499), and taurine to hydrogen sulfide (DsrAB, 228; AsrAB, 284). Nitrate respiration fails a second, independent test: K00370 is named by KEGG as nitrate reductase / nitrite oxidoreductase, one accession for two opposite reactions, so it cannot license a directed claim.
effect: A genome encoding a complete denitrification pathway scores negative on everything in this layer. Curate the part of the chemistry that ends before the acceptor: nitrate assimilation ends at ammonium and both taurine capabilities end at sulfite. Reversing this is an architectural decision needing its own completeness contract.

summary: GlcNAc and sialic acid degradation now declare the ammonium their deaminase liberates
rationale: Both capabilities end at RHEA:12172, the glucosamine-6-phosphate deaminase, whose entire purpose is to remove the amino group. Under the nitrogen-anchor rule they qualify to declare AMMONIUM as an output boundary, which they previously could not because gifter had no nitrogen anchor.
evidence: RHEA:12172 is alpha-D-glucosamine 6-phosphate + H2O = beta-D-fructose 6-phosphate + ammonium, and it is the terminal reaction of route GLCNAC_KINASE and of the sialic acid route.
effect: Two rows in gift_anchors.tsv and the nitrogen_acquisition role on both GIFTs. No route, reaction, system, component or marker changed, and no call changed. The two host-glycan foraging capabilities are now also nitrogen sources and compose into ammonium assimilation.

summary: The carnitine dehydrogenase route makes glycine betaine, not trimethylamine, and is a separate GIFT
rationale: The curation proposal treated CntAB and the CdhA/CdhC dehydrogenase route as two alternative routes of one carnitine-to-trimethylamine capability, on the strength of KEGG naming CdhC a trimethylamine transferase. Checking the reaction against Rhea before curating showed the product is the betainyl thioester and no free amine is released.
evidence: RHEA:47044 is 3-dehydrocarnitine + acetyl-CoA = N,N,N-trimethylglycyl-CoA + acetoacetate, and RHEA:45716 is N,N,N-trimethylglycyl-CoA + H2O = glycine betaine + CoA + H(+). Neither releases trimethylamine. CntAB alone completes in 271 bacteria and the dehydrogenase route in 944; they overlap in 32.
effect: Two GIFTs instead of one with two routes. carnitine_degradation_trimethylamine claims trimethylamine release from 271 genomes rather than from 972, which is the narrowing. carnitine_to_betaine composes into betaine demethylation through the BETAINE anchor, so carnitine still reaches glycine by composition.

summary: Phenylethylamine and hypotaurine degradation are refused on marker specificity
rationale: Both were elements of distillR bundle D06 and both fail the first clause of the evidence test: no marker matches the specificity of the compound the trait is named for.
evidence: Phenylethylamine: K00276 is by KEGG's own name a primary-amine oxidase (975 bacteria) and K00274 a monoamine oxidase (1704); both act on tyramine, histamine and putrescine, so neither can identify the amine. K00146, phenylacetaldehyde dehydrogenase, is substrate-specific but is the wrong step. Hypotaurine: K00485, the only orthology group naming hypotaurine, has zero bacterial members, and the legacy definition used taurine-pyruvate aminotransferase plus a generic aldehyde dehydrogenase, which cannot distinguish the two compounds. Two further refusals on the same clause: the urea amidolyase route, whose fused orthology group K14541 has zero bacterial members, and the creatinine deiminase route, whose first marker K01485 is a cytosine/creatinine deaminase carried by 2702 genomes mostly for the cytosine activity.
effect: No GIFT is created for either compound. Accepting a primary-amine oxidase for phenylethylamine would have damaged every other amine trait the same accession matches, which is invariant 16 exactly.

summary: Twelve aerobic aromatic ring catabolism GIFTs, built around the catechol and 3-oxoadipyl-CoA convergence nodes
rationale: The requested layer was KEGG's Xenobiotics biodegradation module category. Twenty-four candidates were tested and ten were refused or deferred, so what is curated here is the aromatic core that survived: three peripheral entries into catechol, the two ring-cleavage strategies, the shared lower routes, the aerobic phenylacetate route, and the phenylpropanoid node. Every route has a Rhea master at every step and a KEGG module or pathway boundary to compare against.
evidence: Prevalence measured against 11 949 KEGG genomes on 2026-08-18: benzoate to catechol complete in 718, catechol ortho-cleavage in 873, catechol meta-cleavage in 312, the phenylacetate core in 950, the phenylpropanoate chain in 91. All 67 EC numbers spanning the layer returned a Rhea master. Full assessment in inst/doc/proposal-aromatic-degradation.md.
effect: Twelve new GIFTs, twelve new anchors, thirty new reactions and forty-nine new markers. Broadens only: no existing call changes except through the separate acetaldehyde dehydrogenase entry.

summary: Four KEGG module boundaries were cut differently, because a module ORs substrates or duplicates a shared segment
rationale: A KEGG module is not a GIFT. M00569 and M00545 both bundle a shared lower route that five modules duplicate, so it is curated once as oxopentenoate_degradation and composed through the 2-oxopent-4-enoate anchor. M00545 ORs two different input substrates into one module, which gifter cannot do because a route must connect the GIFT's own declared boundaries, so it becomes three GIFTs around the dihydroxyphenylpropanoate node. M00878 and M00568 both end in the same thiolysis, curated once as oxoadipyl_coa_thiolysis. M00548 names benzene as its substrate but its marker set is a phenol 2-monooxygenase, so only the phenol reaction is claimed.
evidence: KEGG module DEFINITION lines and REACTION lists retrieved 2026-08-18; Rhea masters for every step confirm which reaction each marker set catalyses.
effect: The relations recorded in gift_xrefs state each difference: subset_of where gifter cuts shorter, overlaps for the phenol case, equivalent only where the boundaries genuinely agree.

summary: K07104 is refused as evidence of catechol 2,3-dioxygenase; K00446 and NCBIfam TIGR03211 are accepted instead
rationale: Both KEGG orthologues carry the same EC number, but they do not describe the same thing. Accepting the broad one would put a marker in the database that fires in genomes with no aromatic catabolism at all, and it would be available to every future GIFT declaring this activity, not only to this one.
evidence: K07104 is assigned in 2081 of 11 949 KEGG genomes, led by Bacillus (161), Streptococcus (105), Staphylococcus (100) and Listeria (48); only 276 of those genomes carry any lower meta pathway gene. K00446 is assigned in 335 genomes, led by aromatic degraders.
effect: catechol_meta_cleavage calls rest on the specific orthologue. Genomes carrying only K07104 are negative.

summary: Shared ferredoxin and reductase subunits are deliberately not curated as components of Rieske oxygenase systems
rationale: enzyme_component has no required flag, so every curated component is a hard AND. The electron-transfer subunits of ring-hydroxylating oxygenases are interchangeable between systems and systematically under-annotated, so requiring them would report an annotation gap as a missing capability. The substrate-determining subunits are curated instead, and the omission is stated in each system description.
evidence: Catalytic against electron-transfer annotation in KEGG: anthranilate andAc 281 against andAa 101; phthalate pht3 279 against pht2 99; naphthalene ferredoxin 216 against reductase 86.
effect: Affects the benzoate, anthranilate and phenylpropanoate oxygenase systems. The phenol hydroxylase and the phenylacetyl-CoA epoxidase keep all their subunits, because there the components are the enzyme rather than shared carriers.

summary: Two alternative acylating acetaldehyde dehydrogenase systems added to RHEA:23288
rationale: The lower meta-cleavage route ends in the same reaction ethanol formation already uses. MhpF and XylQ are standalone counterparts of the AdhE aldehyde domain and genuinely catalyse it, so they are curated as alternative systems of the shared reaction rather than duplicated.
evidence: KEGG orthology K04073 (1277 genomes) and K18366 (328), both annotated to EC 1.2.1.10, the EC of the existing reaction.
effect: Checked rather than assumed, and the answer was no call changes: ethanol formation's second reaction rests on adhE alone, and a genome carrying adhE already satisfied the first, so no genome's ethanol call moves. The systems matter to the aromatic lower route, which has no adhE.

summary: The aromatic_compound substrate class now covers ring-cleavage products as well
rationale: Three of the new GIFTs act on compounds that are no longer aromatic: 2-oxopent-4-enoate, 3-oxoadipate and its CoA thioester. They exist only because a ring was opened, and classifying them as organic acids would split one degradation funnel across two substrate classes.
evidence: The class was registered by the aromatic biosynthesis layer for benzenoid and heteroaromatic compounds and their branchpoint precursors; this extends the same reasoning downstream.
effect: No existing classification changes; the definition is widened, not redirected.

summary: Nine ring-hydroxylating dioxygenase traits are refused on marker specificity, and five more on evidence availability
rationale: Toluene, benzene, xylene, cumate, p-cymene, biphenyl, carbazole, naphthalene and terephthalate degradation are each named for a substrate recognised in the active site of a Rieske oxygenase, and no marker resolves it. KEGG's own orthologue names admit the promiscuity, and InterPro offers only the family signature. Unlike the butyrate case, no namespace change rescues them. Anaerobic toluene, benzoyl-CoA and cyclohexanecarboxylate degradation are refused on prevalence, caffeine because the reductase its demethylases require has no orthology group at all, and salicylate and phthalate degradation are deferred until the protocatechuate node is curated.
evidence: KEGG orthology prevalence at the bottleneck step: carbazole 1 genome, caffeine 2, xylene 7, terephthalate 8, cymene 10, cumate 11, biphenyl 13, naphthalene 12, anaerobic toluene 12, benzoyl-CoA 16, cyclohexanecarboxylate 24. InterPro returns IPR001663 and PS00570, both substrate-blind, for every dioxygenase alpha subunit searched.
effect: No GIFT is curated for any of them. The register is inst/doc/proposal-aromatic-degradation.md; the benzoate and phenylpropanoate GIFTs carry the specificity statements that follow from it.

summary: The fifteen remaining proteinogenic amino acids curated as eighteen composable biosynthesis GIFTs
rationale: gifter covered five amino acids and the aspartate trunk; every other family entry point was already an anchor, and four of them -- L-aspartate, chorismate, L-glutamine and 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate -- were declared as inputs that no GIFT produced. Six boundaries depart from the KEGG modules, each at a branchpoint where genomes measurably differ: meso-diaminopimelate separates the peptidoglycan precursor from lysine and lets the four acylation routes become one capability (75.3 per cent of bacterial genomes against 51.4, 5.6, 6.8 and 17.2 for the modules read separately); 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate and 2-oxobutanoate separate valine, leucine and isoleucine, which KEGG fuses because the enzymes are shared; and L-glutamine is curated as its own capability although glutamine synthetase also appears inside ammonium assimilation, because the amide nitrogen is consumed by four other GIFTs.
evidence: KEGG orthology over the 10151 bacterial genomes of KEGG release 2026-08-18 for every route count; KEGG modules M00015, M00016, M00019, M00023 to M00028, M00432, M00525 to M00527, M00535, M00570 and M00844 for pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for all 66 new reactions, their direction and their KEGG and EC cross-references; ChEBI release 253 for the fourteen new anchors. Full assessment in inst/doc/proposal-amino-acid-metabolism.md.
effect: Eighteen new GIFTs, fourteen new anchors, twenty-five routes, 66 reactions and 98 new KO markers. Pantothenate, folate, menaquinone, pyrimidine and pyridoxal phosphate biosynthesis stop being nodes whose inputs nothing produces, and the aspartate family now reaches lysine. No existing GIFT call changes: no existing route, system, component or marker was edited.

summary: The final transamination of phenylalanine and tyrosine biosynthesis accepts the aspartate and branched-chain aminotransferases
rationale: KEGG requires TyrB (K00832) or the fungal Aro8 (K00838) for the last step of both aromatic amino acids. Requiring them calls phenylalanine biosynthesis in 2296 bacterial genomes and tyrosine in 1558, while the aryl skeleton that discriminates the traits is present in 7796 and 5893. The aspartate and branched-chain aminotransferases transaminate aromatic 2-oxo acids, and accepting them recovers 7733 and 5852 -- so the step carries almost no information, which is a statement about the transaminase and not about the pathway. It is kept required because it is real chemistry, and the specificity of the claim rests on the skeleton, which is separately evidenced.
evidence: KEGG orthology counts over 10151 bacterial genomes, 2026-08-18: skeleton alone 7796 and 5893, with the KEGG transaminase 2296 and 1558, with the widened set 7733 and 5852.
effect: K00812, K00813, K11358, K00826 and K05821 become accepted evidence for the aromatic transamination components. The same accessions already evidence aspartate biosynthesis and the branched-chain transaminations, which is chemically true of the enzymes and does not equate the traits, because each 2-oxo acid skeleton is separately required.

summary: The amino donor of a transamination is never declared as an anchor; the nitrogen source of an assimilation is
rationale: L-glutamate is a co-substrate of nearly every reaction in the amino acid layer. Declaring it wherever it is consumed would give sixteen new GIFTs an input edge from one node and reduce the composition graph to a star around it. The rule keeps L-glutamate as an anchor only where its carbon skeleton becomes the product -- proline, ornithine and glutamine -- and admits AMMONIUM only under the nitrogen-anchor rule already recorded for the nitrogen layer. It is the nitrogen analogue of the sulfur decision the methionine and cysteine GIFTs encode, and it follows the co-substrate rule recorded as DBC-20260818-COSUBSTRATE-ANCHORS.
evidence: Applied to the eighteen biosynthesis GIFTs of this release: three declare L-glutamate, and the twelve that merely transaminate do not. Applied in the other direction to the ten catabolic GIFTs, every one that liberates ammonium declares it.
effect: No call changes. The rule is what keeps gift_graph() readable at 119 GIFTs, and it is the reason alanine and asparagine biosynthesis declare only their carbon precursor although their routes differ in nitrogen source.

summary: Ten amino acid degradation and transformation capabilities curated, including the first Stickland content
rationale: gifter had no amino acid degradation content of any kind. The ten curated here are those whose markers are specific enough for the trait as named: the arginine deiminase pathway, histidine degradation, threonine and serine deamination, glutamate decarboxylation to GABA, tryptophanase, methionine gamma-lyase, cysteine desulfidation, and the two Stickland reductases. Threonine deamination is curated once, as catabolism, and isoleucine biosynthesis composes from the 2-oxobutanoate anchor rather than repeating the reaction; the resulting chain crosses modes, which the composition rule anticipates.
evidence: KEGG orthology over 10151 bacterial genomes: arginine deiminase pathway 1733, histidine degradation 3688, threonine deaminase 7742, serine dehydratase 6922, glutamate decarboxylase 1684, tryptophanase 741, methionine gamma-lyase 2320, dedicated cysteine desulfidases 2365, complete glycine reductase 128, proline reductase with racemase 90. Rhea release 141 for all fifteen new reactions, including RHEA:12232 and RHEA:12737 for the two selenoprotein reductases.
effect: Ten new GIFTs and five new anchors. Hydrogen sulfide gains a producer, so the two sulfide-dependent biosynthesis GIFTs stop being fed by nothing; ammonium gains eight further producers; and the amino acid layer connects to the fermentation layer through pyruvate. No existing GIFT call changes.

summary: Cysteine desulfidation is evidenced by dedicated desulfidases only, and is knowingly under-called
rationale: Microbial hydrogen sulfide from cysteine is carried out by many PLP enzymes as a side activity -- cystathionine beta-lyase, cystathionine gamma-lyase, MalY, CyuA. Accepting those markers would raise the count from 2365 to over 4000 genomes and destroy the claim, because K01760 is already curated as evidence for cysteine biosynthesis through transsulfuration: every transsulfuration genome would become a sulfide producer. The trait is therefore curated with the dedicated desulfidase orthology groups only.
evidence: K20021, K26607 and K28981 in 2365 of 10151 bacterial genomes; K01760 in 4117, already curated as evidence for cysteine_biosynthesis_homocysteine.
effect: cysteine_degradation_sulfide is negative in genomes whose only cysteine-lyase evidence is a promiscuous PLP enzyme. What would change the decision is a protein family separating desulfidase-competent sequences from the biosynthetic enzymes.

summary: Acetyl phosphate declared as an anchor, because glycine reductase has no other product to declare
rationale: The nitrogen layer met this question from the taurine route and left the intermediate internal, recording the missing edge. That resolution is not available here: source validation requires every metabolic GIFT to declare an output anchor, and acetyl phosphate is the sole product of the Stickland glycine reduction. Declaring it is therefore the condition of curating the trait at all.
evidence: RHEA:12232 releases acetyl phosphate, ammonium and phosphate and nothing else. acetate_interconversion continues to hold the same molecule internally between phosphotransacetylase and acetate kinase.
effect: ACETYL_PHOSPHATE becomes an output-only anchor, on the precedent of GLYOXYLATE, TRIMETHYLAMINE and SULFITE. No edge to acetate formation is created, because acetate_interconversion does not declare the molecule; that edge appears only if that GIFT is re-cut.

summary: L-aspartate and L-glutamine are marked as biomass building blocks
rationale: Both were curated as biomass_essential = no when they existed only as input boundaries: aspartate as the head of the aspartate trunk, glutamine as the amide donor of pyrimidine and pyridoxal phosphate biosynthesis. Both are proteinogenic amino acids, so a growing cell must obtain or synthesise them, which is exactly what the facet says. The oversight only became visible when the amino acid layer gave both a producer, because gift_profile derives auxotrophy_indicator from this facet and the two capabilities were reporting as though nothing depended on them.
evidence: The facet definition in facet_terms.tsv: a building block a growing cell must obtain or synthesise. The eighteen other proteinogenic amino acid anchors in the database already carry yes.
effect: gift_profile.auxotrophy_indicator becomes true for aspartate_biosynthesis and glutamine_biosynthesis, so all twenty proteinogenic amino acids are covered. No Boolean call changes: the facet is read by the derived profile only.

summary: Mercury detoxification curated as a defense GIFT, with MerA-dependent reduction the only required function
rationale: Hg(II) reduction is real chemistry with a Rhea master, but it is not a directed conversion between nutrient anchors, so no mode describes it honestly: catabolic would claim carbon or energy metabolism, interconversion would claim a reversibility the cell never uses, and transport describes only the merT and merP part. Inventing a fifth mode for one trait would put mercury into the anchor graph as edges through metal-ion anchors that mean nothing. The defense contract already covers a chemical challenge, and the machinery model supplies exactly the required and accessory distinction the mer operon needs. Reduction alone is required because a genome carrying merA detoxifies the Hg(II) that reaches its cytoplasm; requiring merT and merP would refuse such genomes on an operon architecture that varies, since merC and merE substitute for the pair in several lineages.
evidence: MerA K00520 with NCBIfam TIGR02053; MerT K08363 with MerP K08364, MerC K19058, MerE K19059; MerR K08365; MerB K00221. RHEA:23856 for the reduction, run in reverse by MerA, and RHEA:18777 for the organomercurial lyase. The assessment is inst/doc/proposal-aromatic-degradation.md, section 8.8.
effect: mercury_detoxification is positive on merA evidence alone, and is the first defense GIFT that is not anti-phage. The three accessory functions are reported as unsupported without changing the call. No metabolic GIFT, anchor, route or reaction is touched, and no existing call changes.

summary: defense_class gains chemical_detoxification, named for the mechanism rather than for the metal or the phenotype
rationale: defense_class is single-valued and partitions the defense type, so the value chosen here is the bucket every future defense GIFT falls into exactly once, and the way to choose it is to write out what each candidate name would have to hold. A resistance class was rejected on three grounds: its roster is mostly not defense GIFTs, since metal efflux is transport, MerR and CmtR are regulatory and lipid A modification is structural; resistance is an outcome, which gifter claims of no GIFT and which this GIFT's own description explicitly disclaims; and invariant 18 puts phenotypic descriptions in a derived layer. metal_detoxification was rejected as too narrow to be worth a partition, leaving three curatable members ever. Naming the class for the mechanism instead admits a populated roster whose members are all markable.
evidence: ArsM has no orthology group; chrR K19784 is defined as a generic NAD(P)H:quinone dehydrogenase and does not resolve chromate; ArsC K00537 produces As(III), which is more toxic than the As(V) it consumes, so the detoxifying step is the ArsB efflux that a detoxification class excludes. The curated vocabulary already carries the precedent: restriction_modification and crispr_cas are both anti-phage and were deliberately not merged into a phage_resistance class. The rosters are in inst/doc/proposal-aromatic-degradation.md, section 10.6.
effect: Future candidates in this class include tellurite methylation (TehB), Cu(I) oxidation (CueO), superoxide and peroxide removal, nitrosative defense, and methylglyoxal and formaldehyde disposal. Efflux, sequestration and repair are excluded by the definition, so an arsenite-efflux GIFT would need a different class. If the axis of which challenge a system acts against is ever wanted, it is a separate multi-valued facet, not a re-cut of this one.

summary: NF033555, the InterPro accessions and merD are refused as mer evidence
rationale: NF033555 and IPR004927 name MerB, and IPR021179 names MerA, more specifically than any accepted accession does. They are not curated because gifter's evidence layer recognises KO, EC, PFAM, TIGRFAM, CAZY and CUSTOM_HMM only: an NF or IPR accession would be stored and never matched, which is worse than leaving it out, because a curator reading the component would see evidence that can never fire. TIGR02053 carries the same claim for MerA in an accepted namespace and is curated in its place; MerB is left on K00221 alone. merD K19057 is refused on different grounds, which are biological: it modulates MerR-driven transcription as a co-regulator rather than activating the promoter, and evidence rows are alternatives within a component, so accepting it would let a genome carrying no activator claim the induction function.
evidence: R/evaluation.R infers and normalises those six namespaces and no others. InterPro records TIGR02053 as integrated into IPR021179 and NF033555 as not integrated into any InterPro entry, both retrieved 2026-08-19.
effect: The organomercurial lysis function is evidenced by K00221 only, and the induction function by K08365 only. Extending the namespace vocabulary to NCBIfam NF accessions or to InterPro is a code change carrying its own evaluation contract and its own confidence ordering, not a content decision, and it needs a second demonstrated need before it is worth making.

summary: The upper oxidative TCA segment is cut at isocitrate and the glyoxylate bypass is curated without duplicated reactions
rationale: Isocitrate is a real branchpoint: oxidative decarboxylation and isocitrate lyase are alternative fates, and keeping it internal forced a bypass GIFT either to repeat citrate synthase and aconitase or to start at an undeclared boundary. The re-cut makes each chemical claim atomic. The bypass ends at succinate and malate and composes back to oxaloacetate through existing segments; glyoxylate remains internal because the complete route both makes and consumes it.
evidence: Rhea release 141: RHEA:13245 and RHEA:18181, with CHEBI:15562 for D-threo-isocitrate. KEGG module M00012, verified 2026-08-20, defines K01637 followed by K01638 or the two-reaction K19282 implementation. K01639 is N-acetylneuraminate lyase and is refused. Full assessment in inst/doc/proposal-central-metabolic-cycles.md and inst/doc/proposal-next-gift-release.md.
effect: acetyl_coa_to_oxoglutarate is replaced by acetyl_coa_to_isocitrate plus isocitrate_to_oxoglutarate. Existing complete upper-TCA marker sets now support two atomic calls instead of one bundled call. glyoxylate_bypass is new on K01637 plus K01638, and a second derived named cycle appears without affecting any member's Boolean call.

summary: Nitrogen fixation is curated as dinitrogen-to-ammonium chemistry with complete Mo and V nitrogenase architectures
rationale: Nitrogen fixation is a bounded metabolic capability, but NifH alone cannot license it. The Mo route therefore requires the catalytic/electron-delivery NifHDK system and nitrogenase-specific NifEN and NifB cofactor assembly. The V route separately requires VnfHDGK, VnfEN and NifB. Fe-S supply and folding factors are excluded where housekeeping pathways can substitute; expression, oxygen protection and electron-donor context are not claimed.
evidence: RHEA release 141 RHEA:21448 and RHEA:55543; ChEBI release 253 CHEBI:17997 and CHEBI:28938; KEGG M00175 and K02585/K02587/K02592/K02586/K02588/K02591/K22896-K22899/K22903, verified 2026-08-20. Minimum Mo and alternative-nitrogenase assembly evidence is reviewed in inst/doc/proposal-next-gift-release.md.
effect: nitrogen_fixation becomes callable through two complete routes. NifH alone, incomplete catalytic complexes and cofactor-assembly-only marker sets remain negative. The Fe-only Anf architecture is documented but deferred because current KO evidence cannot state its minimum native architecture without overclaiming.

summary: Assimilatory sulfate reduction is curated as four explicit APS/PAPS and NADPH/ferredoxin routes
rationale: The sulfate-to-sulfide boundary is shared by distinct activation and terminal-reductase implementations. Materialising four minimal routes preserves OR across valid pathways and AND within each. K00390 is not accepted for either branch-defining component because KEGG assigns it both EC 1.8.4.8 and 1.8.4.10; using it would silently make APS and PAPS routes equivalent. Reaction-specific EC evidence keeps the claims separable. Dissimilatory AprAB and DsrAB are excluded.
evidence: Rhea release 141 RHEA:18136, RHEA:24152, RHEA:11724, RHEA:21976, RHEA:13804 and RHEA:23132; ChEBI release 253 CHEBI:16189 and CHEBI:29919; KEGG M00176 and its KO definitions, verified 2026-08-20; the assimilatory APS-reductase literature reviewed in inst/doc/proposal-next-gift-release.md.
effect: assimilatory_sulfate_reduction becomes callable on any one complete route and connects sulfate to the existing sulfide-dependent cysteine and methionine GIFTs. Sulfite made by taurine desulfonation does not create an edge because it remains an internal reaction participant here, not an input boundary.
